clauses.statement: A push commits when the bucket manifest, `<prefix>/manifest.json` listing each key's sha256, size and owner, replaces the copy it read under `If-Match` on that copy's ETag.

clauses.subject: manifest-format
clauses.statement: The bucket manifest and every generation manifest carry `format`, `1` for this layout; a manifest without `format` reads as `1`.

clauses.subject: format-unsupported
clauses.statement: A bucket or generation manifest whose `format` exceeds 1 raises `SyncManifestFormatUnsupported`, naming the key and its format, before the push commits or the pull writes a file.
clauses.why: because a reader rewriting a manifest it parses only in part drops the fields a newer writer added

clauses.subject: generation
clauses.statement: Each manifest commit carries `generation` per {{store.push.generation-floor}} and the project's table pointers as read before it; the push then creates `<prefix>/manifests/gen-<N>.json` holding the committed bytes under `If-None-Match`.
clauses.why: because a restore or a pre-push gate names one committed state, and the live manifest and pointers move on

clauses.subject: generation-floor
clauses.statement: A commit's `generation` is one past the greater of the read manifest's `generation`, absent reading as 0, and the newest `gen-<N>.json` under the prefix.
clauses.why: because a format-1 writer predating the field drops `generation`, and reusing a taken number collides with its immutable copy

clauses.subject: generation-heal
clauses.statement: Before each manifest commit, a push finding no `gen-<N>.json` for the generation of the manifest it read creates it from the bytes it read.
clauses.why: because a commit of N+1 landing while `gen-<N>.json` is absent leaves a gap no later push sees

clauses.subject: generation-conflict
clauses.statement: A push whose create of `gen-<N>.json` meets another commit's bytes raises `SyncGenerationConflict`, naming N, after its manifest commit applied.
clauses.why: because the immutable copy keeps the first commit, and a push reporting success names a state `pull --generation` does not restore

clauses.subject: run-state
clauses.statement: `sync push` and `sync manifest --emit` first write the node's run state to `nodes/<node-id>/run-state.json`: each pipeline's newest run and each cursor row with its commit marker.
clauses.why: because run history and cursors live outside the store root, and a node starting cold otherwise sees neither

clauses.subject: run-state-format
clauses.statement: A run state carries `format`, `1` for this layout; one whose `format` exceeds 1 contributes no run or cursor to a reader.

clauses.subject: pointer-carry
clauses.statement: After its manifest commit, a push publishes each local table pointer whose snapshot is whole and whose {{store.lay-out.ancestors}} name the bucket pointer's, or the bucket pointer names none, by a conditional put keeping the bucket's fence.
clauses.why: because a snapshot a local fold or a build publishes reads on no other node until its pointer reaches the bucket

clauses.subject: pointer-leased
clauses.statement: A push publishes no pointer for a table whose compaction lease a holder keeps unexpired; that holder publishes under its fence.
clauses.why: because the holder publishes under the fence its acquisition raised, and a publish beside it races that commit

clauses.subject: pointer-fenced
clauses.statement: A local pointer carrying a fence below the bucket pointer's stays local, and the push reports it as a warning beside its commit.

clauses.subject: pointer-unrooted
clauses.statement: A local pointer whose snapshot's ancestry ends at a collected manifest before reaching the bucket pointer's snapshot or a root stays local, and the push reports it as a warning beside its commit.
clauses.why: because a publish over a snapshot it may not descend from drops rows the bucket reaches, and a silent keep leaves every other node reading the older snapshot

clauses.subject: pointer-recommit
clauses.statement: A push whose pointer publish the bucket took commits the manifest again, so a generation names a carried pointer only once the bucket's pointer holds it.
clauses.why: because a generation naming a pointer the bucket never held restores a state no node read

clauses.subject: stranded
clauses.statement: A push names on stderr, per owning node, each local key another node owns that the committed bucket manifest neither lists nor tombstones, with the `CONTEXTFUL_NODE_ID` that pushes it.
clauses.why: because a moved store root re-derives the node id, and runs landed under the old one otherwise stay local without a message

clauses.subject: digest-mismatch
clauses.statement: A downloaded object whose digest differs from its entry raises `SyncObjectDigestMismatch` and is discarded.

clauses.subject: convergence
clauses.statement: When a named key disappears mid-download, the pull re-fetches the manifest and retries the shortfall, up to 3 attempts.

clauses.subject: unconverged
clauses.statement: Exhausting those retries raises `SyncPullDidNotConverge`, naming the key that kept moving, and writes no pointer.

clauses.subject: pointer-last
clauses.statement: A pull writes a table's pointer only after every Parquet part of the snapshot it names is home, so no reader meets a pointer ahead of its data.

clauses.subject: tombstone-applied
clauses.statement: A pull deletes the local copy of each key a tombstone names and no entry lists.
clauses.why: because a deletion that never reaches a consumer resurrects once its tombstone ages out

clauses.subject: pointer-advance
clauses.statement: A pull advances a local pointer only to a bucket pointer carrying a higher fence, or the same fence and a later snapshot, and verifies every advancing table before writing any pointer.

clauses.subject: schema-merge
clauses.statement: A pulled `schema.json` differing from the local copy merges into it column by column through {{store.reconcile.incompatible}}'s lattice rather than replacing it.
clauses.why: because rows landed locally carry columns the bucket's copy may lack

clauses.subject: before-run
clauses.statement: With `[sync] pull_before_run = true`, `run start`, `pipeline run`, `mcp` and `serve` pull every table of the bucket into the store before their first read, and a failed pull stops the command.
clauses.why: because a container starting on an empty disk otherwise serves and folds against a store missing every other node's runs

clauses.subject: generation
clauses.statement: `contextful sync pull --generation <N>` reads `gen-<N>.json` in place of the bucket manifest, downloads each listed key in scope at its listed digest, and writes exactly that generation's pointers, whatever their fence.

clauses.subject: generation-absent
clauses.statement: A generation the bucket holds no `gen-<N>.json` for raises `SyncGenerationAbsent`, naming N and the newest generation, and writes nothing.
clauses.why: because a restore falling back to another generation reads a state nobody named

clauses.subject: generation-diverged
clauses.statement: A generation pull into a store holding a syncable file in scope that the generation does not list raises `SyncGenerationDiverged`, naming the file, and writes nothing.
clauses.why: because a kept unlisted run adds rows the generation never held, and deleting it loses unpushed work

clauses.subject: generation-schema
clauses.statement: A generation pull takes each `schema.json` as the bucket holds it, merged per {{store.pull.schema-merge}}, never refusing on its generation digest.
clauses.why: because the lattice keeps every column an earlier generation carried, and the merged copy replaces the old one in the bucket

clauses.subject: generation-run-state
clauses.statement: A generation pull holds no `nodes/<node-id>/run-state.json` to {{store.pull.generation-diverged}}: one the generation does not list stays as it is, and any other unlisted file under `nodes/` meets that refusal.
clauses.why: because a run state summarizes history outside the store root, and a restore predating it otherwise refuses every node that pushed since

clauses.subject: run-state-cursor
clauses.statement: A run opening where a pulled run state records a commit marker for its pipeline and table newer than every local one resumes from that marker's cursor.
clauses.why: because a collected run takes its manifest's cursor out of the bucket, and a cold node otherwise re-reads the source from its start

clauses.subject: inconclusive
clauses.statement: An unsupported-method response, a forbidden response or a transport error raises `SyncProbeInconclusive` and counts as capability not demonstrated.

clauses.subject: unproven
clauses.statement: Declaring `cas` against a backend the probe did not demonstrate raises `SyncCoordinationUnproven` and stops the push.

clauses.subject: sentinel
clauses.statement: The probe creates a sentinel under `_contextful/cas-probe/` and demonstrates `cas` when a second create and a stale `If-Match` both fail and a current `If-Match` replaces it, deleting the sentinel after.

clauses.subject: network-volume
clauses.statement: A filesystem bucket whose mount type is not apfs, hfs, ext4, xfs, btrfs, zfs, tmpfs or overlay resolves `single-writer` without the sentinel, naming the mount type, and a declared `cas` there meets {{store.probe.unproven}}.
clauses.why: because the bucket's advisory lock is not a guarantee across the clients of a network share, and a sentinel run from one client cannot observe another

clauses.subject: tombstone-owner
clauses.statement: A tombstone whose owner differs from the owner of the entry it names raises `SyncTombstoneForeign`, and the merge keeps the entry.

clauses.subject: tombstone-ttl
clauses.statement: A tombstone leaves the manifest 30 d after its `deleted_at`.

clauses.subject: retries
clauses.statement: `[sync] push_retries` bounds the re-commit loop, defaulting to 5 attempts.

clauses.subject: exhausted
clauses.statement: Exhausting those retries raises `SyncManifestRebaseExhausted`, reports every uploaded object as already in the bucket, and asks for a re-run.

clauses.subject: cursor-recency
clauses.statement: Resolving a cursor by whichever copy was written last raises `SyncCursorConflict`; a cursor resolves through its commit.

clauses.subject: scoped-union
clauses.statement: A merge takes each local entry this writer owns or no node owns, and from the remote every other entry; a remote entry it owns and no longer holds leaves with a tombstone.

clauses.subject: ownership
clauses.statement: A key's owner is read off the key: a run directory's node segment, a request-ledger file's node, a commit log's node directory, or a run state's node directory. Every other key is unowned and propagates no deletion.

clauses.subject: ttl
clauses.statement: A lease is granted for 10 min.

clauses.subject: renewal
clauses.statement: A holder renews every 200 s by `If-Match` replace on the ETag it holds.

clauses.subject: clock-skew
clauses.statement: Bucket leasing assumes the clocks of two machines differ by 30 s or less, and every expiry judgment reads the judging machine's monotonic clock.
clauses.why: because correctness rests on the fence, and the skew bound only sets how early a holder stops committing

clauses.subject: held
clauses.statement: A run finding an unexpired lease raises `LeaseHeld`, naming the holder and the expiry, is skipped, and is attempted again at the next reconciliation tick.

clauses.subject: stale-fence
clauses.statement: A commit-log create, pointer replace or catalog `UPDATE` losing its condition to a higher fence raises `LeaseFenced`, and the run or snapshot it carried stays unreadable.

clauses.subject: not-held
clauses.statement: Releasing a lease another node holds raises `LeaseNotHeld` and leaves the object untouched.

clauses.subject: cursor-kind
clauses.statement: A cursor whose kind takes no lease reaching `cursors/` raises `LeaseCursorKindMismatch`.

clauses.subject: local-node
clauses.statement: A bucket lease attempted under the node id `local` raises `LeaseNodeIdLocal`, logging the variable that sets a node id; that machine keeps the machine lease.

clauses.subject: acquire
clauses.statement: Acquisition creates the lease object under `If-None-Match`, or replaces an expired or released one under `If-Match` on its ETag, the fence one past the object's.

clauses.subject: pointer-fence
clauses.statement: Taking a table's compaction lease raises the fence stored in its bucket pointer, so a publish carrying a lower fence loses its condition.

clauses.subject: network-volume
clauses.statement: Taking a compaction lease on a bucket {{store.probe.network-volume}} resolves to `single-writer` meets {{store.probe.unproven}} naming the mount type, and writes no lease object and no pointer fence.
clauses.why: because a conditional put holding on one machine only lets two machines each take the lease

clauses.subject: commit-log
clauses.statement: Under a machine lease, a run commits by creating the next `cursors/<pipeline-id>/<node-id>/<seq>.json`, and an acquisition creates one carrying its fence; a manifest marked `logged` is readable once that log records it.

clauses.subject: write-refused
clauses.statement: A write verb against a replica raises `ReplicaWriteRefused`, naming the canonical store.

clauses.subject: partial-parquet
clauses.statement: A replica holding a strict subset of a snapshot's Parquet raises `ReplicaPartialParquet` at refresh and leaves that snapshot unpublished.

clauses.subject: missing-index
clauses.statement: A query needing a sidecar or a partition the replica lacks raises `ReplicaMissingIndex`, naming the refresh that supplies it.

clauses.subject: sensitive-refused
clauses.statement: A refresh requesting a replicate-off table raises `ReplicaSensitiveTable`; the consumer reads through the proxying face.

clauses.subject: connection-views
clauses.statement: A session's connection issues one create-or-replace view per table the manifests name, each scanning {{store.reconcile.explicit-file-list}}, once per connection; statements reuse it under {{read.cache.session-pool}}. No view directory exists on disk.

clauses.subject: declaration-set
clauses.statement: The face registers the tables of {{store.declare.declaration-set}}, so a `primary_key` a pipeline file declares reaches {{store.declare.dedup-view}} on the operator verb and the tool server alike.

clauses.subject: engine
clauses.statement: The executor is an embedded columnar SQL engine, linked into every profile that serves reads, reading Parquet natively in standard SQL. An external process reads the same files with the engine uninstalled.

clauses.subject: quiet-table
clauses.statement: A quiet table registers as {{store.declare.empty-run}}. A read of it returns an empty result, never a missing-relation fault.

clauses.subject: bare-name
clauses.statement: A bare table name in any read — a caller statement, a template body, a ranking arm, a file preview — resolves to the caller's registered relation, which carries the caller's restriction.

clauses.subject: tool-set
clauses.statement: The face exposes a closed tool set: `context.describe`, `context.query`, `context.execute_query` for templates, `context.files` and `context.file` over committed data files, `corpus.retrieve` for ranked reads across a prefix, and `memory.recall` for keyed claim reads.

clauses.subject: bound-arguments
clauses.statement: Every read tool but `memory.recall`, each template tool included, admits `as_of` and `valid_as_of` and echoes {{store.bound-time.echo}}; {{store.bound-time.valid-as-of}} wraps only the tables the read touches.
clauses.why: because a session registers every granted table, and wrapping one declaring no pair refuses reads that never name it

clauses.subject: bound-listing
clauses.statement: `context.files` and a `context.describe` naming no table select under `as_of` alone; each ignores `valid_as_of` and echoes only its `as_of` part.
clauses.why: because valid time narrows rows, and a listing returns files and table names, never rows

clauses.subject: describe-payload
clauses.statement: `context.describe` returns row count, schema fingerprint, description, per-column hints, declared indexes, partition scheme, `limits.max_rows`, zone label, lexicon and example queries.

clauses.subject: describe-zone
clauses.statement: `context.describe` reports the session zone as `session_zone`, and per table, listed or described, `zone_admitted`: whether the table's effective allow-set admits that zone.

clauses.subject: advertised-is-enforced
clauses.statement: A table's published `limits` block lists a bound exactly when the engine applies it.
clauses.why: because a published number and a delivered guarantee cannot disagree when one derives from the other

clauses.subject: template-projection
clauses.statement: Every manifest template projects into a tool named by its identifier, whose declared positional parameters form a typed schema with every field required.

clauses.subject: file-listing
clauses.statement: `context.files` returns store-root-relative paths for the tables the caller reads, and a table outside that set contributes no path.

clauses.subject: file-preview-target
clauses.statement: `context.file` resolves a path to its `(table, run_id)` and reads it through that table's registered relation. A snapshot part, a traversal, an absolute path or a ledger file raises `FilePreviewNotATable`.

clauses.subject: ledger-relation
clauses.statement: Each table's per-run request ledger registers as the child relation `<table>__requests`, holding identifiers, connector, method, host, status and timing of mediated outbound calls.

clauses.subject: scoped-ledger
clauses.statement: The child relation registers on the owner read alone: a credential carrying no tenant scope, over a table carrying no row policy. Naming a closed ledger raises `LedgerNotTenantScoped`, stating what closed the relation.

clauses.subject: lexicon-surface
clauses.statement: The describe payload carries the store's numeric-identifier and badge vocabulary. Aliases, time-window phrases and distillation examples stay on the serving side.

clauses.subject: reserved-relation
clauses.statement: The engine's reserved table namespaces register like any other relation, with no privileged path underneath.

clauses.subject: network-transport
clauses.statement: `contextful serve --http <addr> --audience <aud> --max-in-flight <n>` answers MCP Streamable HTTP at `POST /mcp`: one JSON-RPC message per request, answered as `application/json` by the tool server the stdio transport runs.

clauses.subject: concurrent-statements
clauses.statement: Requests on any number of connections run concurrently, each statement on its own engine connection under {{read.cache.pool-connections}}; a slow statement delays no other request.

clauses.subject: serve-declaration
clauses.statement: A serve with no `--audience`, or no positive `--max-in-flight`, raises `ServeDeclarationMissing` naming the flag and binds no listener; neither ships a default.

clauses.subject: past-ceiling
clauses.statement: A request arriving while the ceiling's count of requests is in flight answers `503` with a `Retry-After` of 1 s and admits nothing.

clauses.subject: connection-ceiling
clauses.statement: An accepted connection holds one of the ceiling's slots from accept until its answer is written; a connection accepted with every slot held answers as {{read.register.past-ceiling}} before its request is parsed, and starts no thread.
clauses.why: because a request head arrives before admission, and a slot taken only after reading it lets an unadmitted caller hold one thread per connection

clauses.subject: per-request-admission
clauses.statement: Each request carries `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`, or `DPoP <credential>` with a `DPoP` proof header, admitted per request under {{authority.verify.possession-binding}} and {{authority.verify.network-bearer}}, so one listener serves many credentials, each reading its own grants.

clauses.subject: credential-missing
clauses.statement: A request carrying no `Authorization` credential raises `HttpCredentialMissing` with `401` and reads no row.

clauses.subject: admission-refused
clauses.statement: A request its admission refuses answers `401` carrying the refusal's identifier, except a full nonce cache, which answers `503` under {{authority.verify.nonce-cache}}.

clauses.subject: per-request-revocation
clauses.statement: Each request re-reads the `--denylist` file, so a credential revoked between two requests is refused on the next with no restart; an unreadable denylist answers `503` and admits nothing.

clauses.subject: stateless-session
clauses.statement: A notification answers `202` with no body. The face holds no protocol session and opens no server stream: a `GET` or `DELETE` on `/mcp` answers `405`, any other path `404`.

clauses.subject: request-body
clauses.statement: A request body over 1 MiB answers `413` and is read no further.
clauses.why: because the listener reads the body before admission, and an unbounded body lets an unadmitted caller hold memory

clauses.subject: health
clauses.statement: `GET /health` answers `200` with the build identity of {{read.embed.build-identity}}, admitting no credential and reading no row.
clauses.why: because a container runtime probes readiness before any caller holds a credential

clauses.subject: single-read-only-statement
clauses.statement: Admitted text parses to exactly one read-only SELECT. Attach, copy, install, load, pragma, set, any schema change, any data modification and a piggybacked second statement raise `StatementNotReadOnly`.

clauses.subject: engine-own-parse
clauses.statement: The guard walks the syntax tree the engine itself serializes for the statement; read-only-ness is a property of that tree, not a keyword blocklist.
clauses.why: because guard and executor cannot disagree about what a text means when they share one parse

clauses.subject: relation-allowlist
clauses.statement: Every base relation names a view registered for this caller or a common table expression the statement declares. A bare file path is a base relation and falls under this rule.

clauses.subject: whole-tree-walk
clauses.statement: The walk covers the entire tree — select-list subqueries, union arms, pivot sources — and a common-table-expression name resolves only within the scope that declares it and the scopes beneath.

clauses.subject: unregistered-relation
clauses.statement: A base relation naming nothing this connection registered is refused by {{authority.refuse.ungranted-table}}, echoing what the statement asked for and no relation of another caller.

clauses.subject: table-function
clauses.statement: A table function anywhere in the tree, and a schema-qualified reach into a system catalog, raise `TableFunctionRefused`.

clauses.subject: statement-provenance
clauses.statement: Admission binds on who authored the text. Operator text — the local command line, template bodies, engine-composed reads — runs raw; capability-token caller text is gated. The raw surface is reachable from no network face.

clauses.subject: quoted-identifiers
clauses.statement: Every schema- or manifest-derived identifier is double-quoted where rendered, admitting any UTF-8 vendor field name as an identifier and never as an expression.

clauses.subject: template-declaration
clauses.statement: A template declares an identifier, one SQL statement, positional parameters written `name:type` over integer, float, string, timestamp and boolean, and an optional row ceiling.

clauses.subject: template-reserved-parameter
clauses.statement: A template parameter named `as_of`, `valid_as_of`, `zone` or `pin` refuses the manifest; those names carry the read's bounds, zone and pin map on every template tool.
clauses.why: because a parameter sharing a read argument's name hides that bound from the template tool

clauses.subject: template-relation-shape
clauses.statement: Manifest validation and face startup refuse a template whose SQL names anything but the store's own tables as plain identifiers, or whose identifier opens with a built-in tool prefix — `context.`, `corpus.` or `memory.` — raising `TemplateNamesForeignRelation`.

clauses.subject: template-binding
clauses.statement: A missing, unknown or type-mismatched argument raises `TemplateArgumentRejected` ahead of execution, with no coercion. Placeholders are `$1`…`$n` or `?` in declaration order, or exactly the declared names.

clauses.subject: query-binding
clauses.statement: `context.query` takes `parameters`, mapping each placeholder name to a `type` among {{read.guard.template-declaration}} types and a `value`. A missing, unused, untyped or mismatched parameter raises `QueryParameterRejected` ahead of execution, with no coercion; bound values reach {{authority.refuse.scope-guard}}.
clauses.why: because a value bound to a placeholder reaches no parser, and the tenant guard decides a bound value as it decides a literal

clauses.subject: startup-time-check
clauses.statement: Template checks are caller-independent and run once at startup; a request pays nothing for them.

clauses.subject: one-projection
clauses.statement: The command line's JSON output, the HTTP face and the tool protocol serialize one projection: `columns`, `rows`, `truncated`, and the optional restriction, resolved-build, provenance, retrieval and time-bound blocks.
clauses.why: because a guarantee landing on one transport and missing on another is worse than a guarantee on none

clauses.subject: row-ceiling
clauses.statement: A per-table row ceiling published as `limits.max_rows` bounds rows delivered, applied at execution with an over-fetch of 1 rows. It bounds no work performed.

clauses.subject: face-ceiling
clauses.statement: Every read on every face, `corpus.retrieve` included, delivers at most 10000 rows: the face ceiling is always a component of {{authority.grant.row-ceiling}}, declared or not, and bounds the candidate window.
clauses.why: because an undeclared ceiling otherwise streams a whole table into one response, and a caller learns of the cut from `truncated` rather than from memory exhaustion

clauses.subject: truncation-is-exact
clauses.statement: `truncated` is set exactly when the over-fetched probe row is present, never by comparing a returned count against a requested limit.

clauses.subject: cell-encoding
clauses.statement: SQL NULL is JSON `null` and nothing else is. Non-finite floats are `"NaN"`, `"inf"`, `"-inf"`; temporal values are ISO-8601 strings, intervals ISO-8601 durations; an enum is its label; a union is its text form.

clauses.subject: bytes-and-vectors
clauses.statement: Binary is padded base64, and a fixed-size float array, a vector column included, is a JSON array holding each element as a float cell.

clauses.subject: nested-values
clauses.statement: A list is a JSON array, and a struct or a map a JSON object keyed by field name or key text, each item, field or value encoded as its own cell.

clauses.subject: wide-number-shape
clauses.statement: A column's JSON encoding follows its SQL type alone: integers of 32 bits or fewer, finite floats and decimals of 15 digits or fewer are numbers; wider integers and decimals are exact decimal strings.
clauses.why: because a wire type that varies with the values on one page breaks a typed client on the next

clauses.subject: type-is-the-cell
clauses.statement: No separate type list rides the envelope; a cell's JSON type is the declaration.

clauses.subject: zero-rows-is-success
clauses.statement: Fewer rows than the requested limit, zero included, is a success.

clauses.subject: match-count
clauses.statement: Match counts ride outside the internals opt-in, reporting how many rows the ranker scored as matching in the same call.

clauses.subject: coverage-is-a-count
clauses.statement: A claim that the corpus lacks coverage of a subject comes from a count over the table with no recency truncation, taken after the full-scan fallback, never from a ranked top score.
clauses.why: because min-max normalization pins the best row at 1.0 and IDF lifts one incidental rare-term mention

clauses.subject: internals-opt-in
clauses.statement: Executed SQL, engine name, applied limit, row count and elapsed milliseconds ride a separate object returned only under `internals: true`, on every read tool and the HTTP face.

clauses.subject: operator-metadata
clauses.statement: Operator-surface table metadata carries column count and backing file list; a row count is an ordinary count query, never a stored field.

clauses.subject: restriction-block
clauses.statement: The restriction block carries the session zone, the incognito flag and one entry per touched relation the zone excludes or column-masks: `table`, `excluded`, `rows_dropped` and `columns_masked`. A read withholding no touched relation omits the block.

clauses.subject: in-band-error
clauses.statement: On the tool protocol a refusal arrives in-band, as a protocol error object or a result flagged as an error under transport success.

clauses.subject: paths-stay-inside
clauses.statement: An ordinary read's result carries no store path. Provenance arrives as columns naming table, run, connector version, ingestion instant and authoring subject.

clauses.subject: operator-verb
clauses.statement: `contextful query --json [--project <name>] [--declaration <path>] [--limit <n>] <sql>` runs one operator statement raw under {{read.guard.statement-provenance}} and prints the {{read.respond.one-projection}} envelope as one JSON line on standard output.

clauses.subject: one-statement
clauses.statement: Text the engine's parser splits into other than exactly one statement raises `QueryNotOneStatement` before any statement runs.
clauses.why: because preparing multi-statement text executes every statement but the last and answers only the last, dropping the earlier results and side effects unseen

clauses.subject: project-relations
clauses.statement: Under a project, every table the store holds or the manifest declares registers under its bare name as its unrestricted base relation at the latest committed state; a quiet table reads as {{read.register.quiet-table}}.
clauses.why: because operator text is the store owner's own, and a restriction bounds a capability-token caller

clauses.subject: discovered-project
clauses.statement: Without `--project`, the project {{store.init.discovery}} finds is the verb's project. When discovery finds none, or the found project's store is absent, no relation registers and the statement runs over no store.
clauses.why: because every other verb reads the nearest `contextful.toml`, and a statement over files or literals needs no store

clauses.subject: project-store
clauses.statement: A `--project` whose `.contextful/context/<project>/` store is absent raises `QueryProjectAbsent`.
clauses.why: because every declared table of an absent store registers as quiet, and an operator reads its zero rows as an answer

clauses.subject: declaration-default
clauses.statement: `--declaration <path>` names the manifest whose declared tables register; without it, the {{store.init.default-declaration}} file does when present, and no manifest otherwise. With no project, `--declaration` refuses by {{store.init.undiscovered}}.

clauses.subject: limit-truncates
clauses.statement: `--limit <n>` bounds rows delivered with the over-fetch of {{read.respond.row-ceiling}}, and sets `truncated` per {{read.respond.truncation-is-exact}}. Without it every row is delivered and `truncated` is false.

clauses.subject: engine-fault
clauses.statement: A statement the engine rejects exits non-zero with the engine's message on standard error and nothing on standard output.
clauses.why: because a caller parsing standard output never mistakes a partial or empty envelope for an answer

clauses.subject: ranked-call
clauses.statement: `corpus.retrieve({prefix, query, query_embedding?, filter?, kinds?, limit?, since?, min_score?, as_of?})` returns the top rows across the item and artifact genres under one prefix, each with a snippet and full provenance. It composes the query surface and memory recall, storing nothing.

clauses.subject: relevance-floor
clauses.statement: A row reaches a caller when its lexical score is null, at least the floor, or its vector score is positive. The floor is 2 tokens for queries of 3 tokens or more, else 1 tokens; a caller minimum overrides.

clauses.subject: content-tokens
clauses.statement: The query text is lowercased and split on non-alphanumeric characters. Stop tokens drop, non-ASCII runs of two or more characters stay, and survivors deduplicate in order.

clauses.subject: token-length-floor
clauses.statement: An ASCII run shorter than 2 chars leaves the content-token set.

clauses.subject: token-cap
clauses.statement: The content-token set holds at most 12 tokens. An empty set omits the relevance predicate.

clauses.subject: script-split-matching
clauses.statement: An all-lowercase-alphanumeric token matches on an ASCII word boundary with an optional plural suffix; a token with any non-ASCII character matches by containment.
clauses.why: because no ASCII word boundary occurs beside an ideograph

clauses.subject: plural-suffix-floor
clauses.statement: A token under 4 chars takes no optional plural suffix.

clauses.subject: text-free-table-scores-null
clauses.statement: A table with no snippet-worthy text column scores lexically null, never zero, and its rows enter by vector score alone.

clauses.subject: candidate-window
clauses.statement: The candidate window is 8 times the requested limit or 200 rows, whichever is larger. Candidates equal to the window report that the ranking saw a recency-ordered slice.

clauses.subject: reserved-columns-project-null
clauses.statement: Reserved projected columns — modality, language, prompt hash, kind — render null for a table lacking them, and its rows stay in the union.

clauses.subject: unsatisfiable-arm-drops
clauses.statement: `filter` maps each caller-named column to a value, an equality, or a value list, a membership, and a row matches every condition. A table lacking a named column drops its arm, never emitting it unfiltered.

clauses.subject: filter-values
clauses.statement: A filter value is a string, a number or a boolean, and a membership list is non-empty; a null, a nested object or list, or an empty list is a malformed condition.

clauses.subject: kinds
clauses.statement: `kinds` lists artifact kind strings and joins the filter as one membership condition on the `kind` column, so a table without that column drops its arm by {{read.retrieve.unsatisfiable-arm-drops}}.

clauses.subject: engine-resolved-date
clauses.statement: The engine resolves each table's publication column itself, outside the caller's filter.

clauses.subject: filter-budget
clauses.statement: A filter holds at most 32 conditions, each membership list at most 256 entries, and its serialized JSON, `kinds` included, at most 16 KiB.

clauses.subject: filter-budget-refusal
clauses.statement: The budget is checked over the whole filter ahead of building any arm; an oversized or malformed condition raises `FilterBudgetExceeded` for the whole read.

clauses.subject: row-key-dedup
clauses.statement: A ranked read keeps per `(table, row key)` only the newest ingestion, and no older copy when the newest misses the relevance floor. The row key is the declared content-hash column, else null, never a digest over projected values.

clauses.subject: row-key-under-mask
clauses.statement: A content-hash column the session masks by `drop`, `truncate`, `bucket`, `range` or any combine keys every row null; one masked by `hash` or `tokenize` alone keys by its digest.
clauses.why: because a mask merging distinct hashes lets a reader's grants decide which rows a table holds

clauses.subject: row-key-stays-internal
clauses.statement: The row key is absent from the outer projection.

clauses.subject: dedup-is-gated
clauses.statement: The deduplicating window function runs under the same condition as the relevance floor, and a browse-shaped read skips it.

clauses.subject: excluded-arm
clauses.statement: An arm whose table the session's zone excludes contributes no candidate, and the ranked response names that table in {{read.respond.restriction-block}}.

clauses.subject: snippet
clauses.statement: A snippet concatenates up to three text columns: label-priority columns — title, summary, description, thesis and kin — first, then prose-worthy columns in schema order.

clauses.subject: identifiers-never-snippet
clauses.statement: Content hashes, URLs, identifiers and instant-valued columns never qualify for a snippet.

clauses.subject: sidecar-generates-candidates
clauses.statement: Each sidecar arm, vector over a query embedding and full-text over the content tokens, adds its top results to the recency window, each re-joined by {{authority.compose.vector-arm}}. Per-row scores equal the exact path's.

clauses.subject: fulltext-probe
clauses.statement: A full-text probe ranks the whole snapshot by BM25 over one should-clause per content token; a token the sidecar's tokenizer splits into several terms matches them at consecutive positions, and an ASCII word token matches its plural as {{read.retrieve.script-split-matching}} does.
clauses.why: because a term outside the recency window is found only by a probe that reads every row's postings

clauses.subject: sidecar-oversampling
clauses.statement: One probe requests 4 times the limit or 64 rows, whichever is larger, and 4 times that where the request carries restriction context.

clauses.subject: sidecar-size-cap
clauses.statement: A sidecar holding more than 64 MiB of stored vectors stays unloaded and the arm takes the exact scan.

clauses.subject: fulltext-sealed-cap
clauses.statement: A sealed full-text sidecar file larger than 256 MiB stays unopened, and its arm adds no candidates.

clauses.subject: sidecar-falls-back
clauses.statement: Any sidecar precondition failure — no snapshot, no matching sidecar, a masked or zone-withheld identifier or indexed column, a classed text column, a dimension or manifest mismatch, an unreadable dump — falls back to the exact scan.

clauses.subject: gain-never-loss
clauses.statement: For one reader the accelerated arm returns a superset of the exact path's rows. Two readers with one query on one snapshot can recall different rows.

clauses.subject: three-legs
clauses.statement: Ranking runs exact cosine similarity over the candidate set, BM25 over a full-text index, and a weighted fusion of the two.

clauses.subject: fusion
clauses.statement: Fusion computes `w_vec · clamp(cosine, 0, 1) + w_lex · minmax(bm25)` with default weights 60 percent and 40 percent. A document absent from one leg scores zero there; ties break by identifier.

clauses.subject: lexical-leg-matches-only
clauses.statement: The BM25 leg ranks a disjunction of should-clauses; a document matching no term is absent. An empty query, candidate set or result yields an empty ranking that falls back to recency order.

clauses.subject: flat-window-full-credit
clauses.statement: A lexical window with no score spread awards every present document full credit.

clauses.subject: question-window-is-a-tier
clauses.statement: A question's timeframe projects a per-row in-window flag against the resolved publication column, and the flag leads the ordering. An out-of-window row sorts down and stays.

clauses.subject: window-anchor-tolerance
clauses.statement: A publication instant more than 24 h past the question's anchor sets the in-window flag false. A null or uncastable value sets it false too, and a basis field names which case applied.

clauses.subject: ordering-casts-first
clauses.statement: Ordering compares publication values as `TIMESTAMPTZ` instants, casting a text value before any comparison.
clauses.why: because a text comparison of two date spellings orders strings, not instants

clauses.subject: retrieval-block
clauses.statement: The `contextful.retrieval` block reports window, candidates_prefloor, candidates, matched, returned, in_window, deduped, padded, floor and since. Each row carries an integer score bounded by the content-token count, the in-window flag and the basis label.

clauses.subject: internal-score-stays-internal
clauses.statement: The lexical engine's own float score never crosses to a caller.
clauses.why: because a corpus-relative number drifts under a consumer's threshold as the corpus changes

clauses.subject: absent-block
clauses.statement: The retrieval block is omitted from every non-ranked statement and from a build with no ranker, and an absent block differs from one reporting zero matches.

clauses.subject: degradation-not-error
clauses.statement: Without the lexical backend linked, ranking substitutes a token fallback scoring each query token over the snippet, recency breaking ties. The result differs in order and still answers.

clauses.subject: fallback-counts-tokens
clauses.statement: Under the fallback every matching token contributes, ranking hyphenated, spaced and possessive phrasings equivalently.

clauses.subject: caller-embedding
clauses.statement: A supplied `query_embedding` adds per-row cosine fused with the lexical leg; omitting one leaves every projected column as the lexical-only path. Without the vector backend it scores only rows the recency window recalled.

clauses.subject: lexical-index-cache
clauses.statement: An opened full-text sidecar is cached on a fingerprint of its table, snapshot, path and key version in a FIFO of 64 entries, so a repeated read opens nothing and a new snapshot opens afresh.

clauses.subject: widened-window-statistics
clauses.statement: Lexical term statistics come from the widened candidate window, so an accelerated arm can order rows differently from the exact path.

clauses.subject: hot-local-parquet
clauses.statement: The retrieval container syncs the current snapshot set to local disk and memory-maps it; object storage stays out of the per-query path.

clauses.subject: cold-start
clauses.statement: A cold retrieval container meets {{topology.publish-hostname.container-readiness}}; a container holding no snapshot adds a whole-store pull before its first answer.

clauses.subject: result-key
clauses.statement: A cached result keys on the token's id, revocation epoch, grants and subject, the session zone and incognito state, each touched relation and the files it reads, the bounds, the statement, its parameter values and the applied row ceiling.

clauses.subject: cache-is-opt-in
clauses.statement: A statement's result caches only when every table it touches declares `result_cache`, a time to live, and none declares `private = true`; an entry expires at the least time to live among them.

clauses.subject: volatile-bypasses
clauses.statement: A statement calling a function the engine marks other than consistent across queries, such as `now()`, `current_timestamp` or `random()`, or a macro reaching one, executes uncached.
clauses.why: because such a call answers differently under an unchanged key, and a hit returns its first answer frozen until the entry expires

clauses.subject: frontier-invalidates
clauses.statement: A commit, fold or request-ledger append on a touched table moves its read frontier, the snapshot and runs its relation reads, so an entry filled before it stops matching. A statement in flight during a fold reads {{store.fold.non-blocking}}.

clauses.subject: budget
clauses.statement: The result cache holds at most the byte budget its process declares, the least recently used entry evicted first; a face declaring no budget caches nothing.

clauses.subject: hit-identical
clauses.statement: A hit returns the response byte-identical to the miss that filled it, restriction block included; under `internals: true` the internals object carries `cache` as `hit` or `miss`.
clauses.why: because a reused answer differing from a computed one is a second projection a caller must reconcile

clauses.subject: keep-warm-is-per-deployment
clauses.statement: A deployment with active traffic keeps its retrieval container warm; one declining keep-warm takes a cold first read.

clauses.subject: session-pool
clauses.statement: `Face` reuses a resolved session and its connections while the whole key holds: admitted authority, token id, revocation epoch, request zone, bounds, pin map, table set, and per granted table its schema digest, pointer, run set and ledger files.

clauses.subject: change-misses
clauses.statement: A committed run, snapshot, schema edit, new table, request-ledger file or token under another id or epoch misses the pool, and the next statement reads the new state on a new connection.

clauses.subject: pool-entries
clauses.statement: The pool holds at most 16 entries, oldest evicted first; a miss evicts the same principal's entries under an older store state.
clauses.why: because connections hold memory per authority, and an entry under a superseded store state is never hit again

clauses.subject: pool-connections
clauses.statement: One pool entry keeps at most 4 connections idle; a concurrent statement past them opens its own and closes it afterwards.
clauses.why: because concurrency on one session is bursty, and an idle connection holds its footer cache in memory

clauses.subject: pin-parameter
clauses.statement: Every read tool admits `pin`, mapping a table name to a build identifier, and resolves that table to the files its build's committed manifest names. An unnamed table resolves to the latest published state.

clauses.subject: pinned-schema
clauses.statement: A pinned table registers under the columns its build's parts carry, so a later build's contract neither adds, drops nor retypes a column of the pinned read or its description.

clauses.subject: null-pin
clauses.statement: A table `pin` maps to `null` resolves as an unnamed table, and a pin map differing from another only by such entries is the same map.

clauses.subject: unknown-build
clauses.statement: An unknown or collected build identifier raises `PinnedBuildUnavailable`, naming the oldest identifier still pinnable. A pin never widens to the latest state.
clauses.why: because a substituted build applied to every remaining query passes the consumer's cross-query comparison and stitches two states

clauses.subject: unregistered-pin
clauses.statement: A pin on a table the session registers no relation for, absent or outside the grants, refuses as {{read.resolve-pin.unknown-build}} on a table publishing no build, in one text for both.
clauses.why: because an answer differing between an absent and an ungranted table discloses the ungranted table's existence

clauses.subject: earlier-bound-wins
clauses.statement: A pin and the store's transaction-time bound are upper bounds on one clock; a table named by both resolves to the earlier.

clauses.subject: resolved-echo
clauses.statement: A response touching a published model carries `contextful.resolved`, mapping each such table to `{build_id, watermark}`, pinned or not and zero rows included; the watermark names, per input table, the snapshot id and the committed runs it omits.

clauses.subject: absent-watermark
clauses.statement: The watermark is null for a materialization carrying none, distinct from a watermark of zero.

clauses.subject: consumer-comparison
clauses.statement: A consumer compares resolved build identifiers across every query of one derivation and fails the derivation where two differ.

clauses.subject: default-embedder
clauses.statement: The embedding capability is a port whose default is deterministic and I/O-free: it hashes token term frequencies into an L2-normalized vector, needing no download, key or network call.

clauses.subject: default-embedder-reach
clauses.statement: The default is a lexical-vector baseline: a paraphrase is orthogonal under it and cross-lingual recall is undefined. Semantic reach comes from the learned in-process model or a caller-supplied query embedding.

clauses.subject: model-identifier
clauses.statement: Every stored vector lands in a {{store.reconcile.binary-and-vector}} column beside an `embedding_model` column naming the model that produced it; index identity and provenance resolve from the rows alone.

clauses.subject: build-identity
clauses.statement: The handshake reports the linked retrieval backends (`duckdb`, `fts`, `hnsw`), connector families (`m365`, `s3`, `wasm`) and faces (`http`, `eval`, `otlp`), composed from the same feature declarations the version output reads.

clauses.subject: required-face
clauses.statement: A client passing `require: [...]` is refused ahead of its first read with `RequiredFaceAbsent` for any name outside the reported set. An engine reporting no set satisfies no requirement.

clauses.subject: absent-read-backend
clauses.statement: Without the embedded SQL engine linked, both read tools raise `ReadBackendAbsent` rather than answering from a narrower path.

clauses.subject: canonical-column
clauses.statement: A table naming a shape and omitting one of its canonical columns raises `MemoryShapeColumnMissing` when the declaration loads.

clauses.subject: undeclared-relation
clauses.statement: A candidate edge whose `rel_type` falls outside the union lands in the dead-letter table and raises `MemoryUndeclaredRelation`; no row is written under the unknown type.

clauses.subject: reserved-relations
clauses.statement: The reserved relation core contains `supports`, `contradicts`, `supersedes`, `about` and `derived_from`; a deployment extends it through `[relation].declared`, and `contextful memory relations rename` rewrites stored edges before removing an old name.

clauses.subject: extract-attempts
clauses.statement: A schema-invalid response is re-prompted with its validation feedback, at most 3 attempts per batch in total.

clauses.subject: dead-letter
clauses.statement: A batch exhausting {{read.synthesize.extract-attempts}} writes the response, template hash and drop reason to the dead-letter table, raises `MemoryExtractExhausted`, and leaves the cursor unadvanced.

clauses.subject: pass-cursor
clauses.statement: A pass reads the source's committed rows its cursor has not recorded, through the writing credential's own session, in batches under {{read.synthesize.prompt-bound}}, recording each batch once its claims commit.

clauses.subject: prompt-bound
clauses.statement: A batch packs fenced rows up to 32 KiB; a fenced row over that bound travels in a batch of its own.
clauses.why: because one oversized row neither stalls the pass nor drags its neighbours past the bound

clauses.subject: row-cap
clauses.statement: A row is fenced at 16384 chars under {{connector.infer.value-cap}}; a truncated row still reaches the model, its batch commits and advances the cursor, and the pass report counts it in `truncated`.
clauses.why: because a silent cut hides that a conclusion rests on a partial row

clauses.subject: attribution
clauses.statement: Every landed claim carries `grant_id`, the chain-final revocation identifier of the credential that wrote it, `agent`, that credential's agent member, and `_authored_by`, its on-behalf-of principal.
clauses.why: because a reader weighs a conclusion by which grant could have produced it

clauses.subject: claim-taint
clauses.statement: A source row carries its own `_taint`, else `ingested:third-party`. Every row a batch commits lands under {{store.reserve.taint}} with the least-trusted label among the batch's rows.
clauses.why: because a row no label vouches for is trusted least, and a claim re-synthesized from claims stays as low as its origin

clauses.subject: cadence
clauses.statement: Each memory shape defaults to an operator-triggered synthesis pass; a deployment schedule for that shape replaces the default, and a pass still advances only through {{read.synthesize.pass-cursor}}.

clauses.subject: confidence-calibration
clauses.statement: A model-emitted confidence is labelled `uncalibrated` until a shape-and-predicate isotonic map trained on settled outcomes lowers held-out Brier score; a validated map supplies the reported calibrated confidence.

clauses.subject: tier
clauses.statement: `tier` is stamped from the write path and grounding, never the payload: a synthesis pass stamps `derived`, a direct write `curated`, a fetched result `researched`, and mixed grounding takes the lowest.

clauses.subject: supersede
clauses.statement: A claim of equal or higher tier retires a live prior of its subject, predicate and scope when both are open-ended or share a valid-from instant: the prior's `valid_to` becomes the claim's `valid_from`, and `superseded_by` names it.

clauses.subject: direct-write
clauses.statement: The direct write accepts claims alone. Naming `memory_episodes`, `memory_entities`, `memory_edges` or `memory_preferences` raises `MemoryDirectWriteShapeRefused`; an entity row enters through the entity upsert.

clauses.subject: observed-at
clauses.statement: `contextful memory write --observed-at <instant>` lands the claim with `valid_from` at that instant; without it, `valid_from` is the write's own instant.

clauses.subject: dedup-key
clauses.statement: `--dedup-key <key>` derives `claim_id` from the key beside the subject, predicate, object and scope, and a write whose `claim_id` the table already holds lands nothing.
clauses.why: because a retried write restates one observation, while one fact observed twice under two keys keeps two validity intervals

clauses.subject: observed-order
clauses.statement: A direct write whose `valid_from` precedes the `valid_from` of an unsuperseded claim of its subject, predicate and scope with another object raises `MemoryObservationOutOfOrder`, and nothing lands.
clauses.why: because retiring the later claim at the earlier instant ends it before it starts, and it then answers at no instant

clauses.subject: citation-live
clauses.statement: A direct write citing a keyed table's row that reads through the writer's session as a version its key has since replaced raises `MemoryCitationNotLive`, and nothing lands.
clauses.why: because such a claim rests on a replaced version from its first read, while a citation no readable row carries lands undigested and recall withholds it

clauses.subject: unscoped-collision
clauses.statement: Direct writes with no scope, equal subject, predicate and valid-from, and different objects record both claim ids in the dead-letter table; neither claim retires the other until an explicit revision resolves the conflict.

clauses.subject: retention-default
clauses.statement: Claims retain their recorded validity until explicit expiry or erasure; ranking decay is opt-in per shape with a declared half-life, and never deletes a claim or changes its validity interval.

clauses.subject: evidence-unresolved
clauses.statement: An unreadable or masked source row, an unknown table, a reference into another memory row, or malformed lineage suppresses the claim and raises `MemoryEvidenceUnresolved`.

clauses.subject: evidence-references
clauses.statement: A claim naming more than 256 entries of evidence is suppressed unresolved, raising `MemoryEvidenceOverflow`.

clauses.subject: evidence-key
clauses.statement: The write landing a claim stamps each citation into a keyed table with a pepper-keyed digest of the cited row's key; recall resolves a citation whose row no longer reads through the digest's live version.

clauses.subject: evidence-key-masked
clauses.statement: A citation whose key column reads masked or nulled by zone in the writer's session carries no digest; a masked or nulled column outside the key leaves the digest stamped.
clauses.why: because a masked key cell digests a value no other session reads, while a cell outside the key plays no part in matching it

clauses.subject: evidence-no-value
clauses.statement: A citation stored in a memory row carries the cited table, run, sequence and key digest, and no cell value of the cited row.

clauses.subject: evidence-stale
clauses.statement: A claim served through its key digest while its cited run and sequence no longer read counts under `stale` in the `contextful.recall` block, which names no claim.

clauses.subject: ranked-arm
clauses.statement: A `corpus.retrieve` arm over a `memory_facts` table serves only live claims — no `superseded_by`, and a `valid_to` null or past the read's anchor — whose evidence passes the gate.

clauses.subject: suppression-count
clauses.statement: A suppressed claim is absent from the rows; the `contextful.recall` block counts suppressions per error identifier and names no claim.
clauses.why: because a count discloses that a conclusion was withheld, never what it concluded

clauses.subject: keyed
clauses.statement: `memory.recall` takes `table`, `subject`, `observed_at`, `as_of_ingest` and `limit`, and returns the claims whose `subject` equals `subject` exactly and whose `valid_from` and `valid_to` cover `observed_at` as {{store.bound-time.valid-as-of}} does.

clauses.subject: keyed-clocks
clauses.statement: `as_of_ingest` bounds the read as {{store.bound-time.as-of}} does; absent, the read takes the latest committed state, and an absent `observed_at` the call's instant. `contextful.bounds` echoes each supplied bound under its argument name, with a per-name `inclusive` map.

clauses.subject: keyed-history
clauses.statement: A claim a successor retired still answers an `observed_at` inside its validity; the keyed read filters on validity alone, never on `superseded_by`.
clauses.why: because the question is what held at that instant, and the retired claim is the answer its interval records

clauses.subject: keyed-gate
clauses.statement: Every keyed claim passes {{read.recall.evidence-unresolved}} and {{read.recall.evidence-references}}, and the response carries {{read.recall.suppression-count}}.

clauses.subject: keyed-window
clauses.statement: The keyed read gates claims in order and stops once it keeps one claim past the row ceiling, so the suppression count covers the claims gated before that stop.
clauses.why: because a one-row recall over a subject with thousands of claims otherwise resolves every claim's evidence

clauses.subject: keyed-order
clauses.statement: Keyed claims order by tier, `curated` first, then `valid_from`, newest first, then `claim_id`; `limit` and the table's ceilings bound them under {{read.respond.row-ceiling}}.

clauses.subject: keyed-not-claims
clauses.statement: A granted `table` declaring a shape other than `memory_facts`, or no memory shape, raises `MemoryRecallNotClaims`.
clauses.why: because a keyed read answers with a claim's subject, validity and evidence, which no other table carries

clauses.subject: stale-revision
clauses.statement: A stale citation remains subject to {{read.recall.keyed-gate}}; only a newly committed source row advancing {{read.synthesize.pass-cursor}} starts synthesis against its live key version.

clauses.subject: usage-ledger
clauses.statement: Each `memory.recall` and ranked memory arm records the ids of claims actually returned in the request ledger, under the caller's admitted authority and the read frontier.

clauses.subject: ambiguous-mention
clauses.statement: A mention matching two canonical identities with no deterministic key separating them is recorded as an ambiguous skip, raises `MemoryEntityAmbiguous`, and dead-letters its candidate claim.

clauses.subject: edge-endpoint
clauses.statement: A candidate edge whose source or target resolves to no identity is dead-lettered, raising `MemoryEdgeEndpointUnresolved`.

clauses.subject: graph-index
clauses.statement: An external graph engine is a derived index of admitted memory edges; an entity or ownership answer resolves through the store's enforced rows at the read frontier.

clauses.subject: ownership-answer
clauses.statement: An artifact's ownership answer returns every attached principal visible to the caller, newest attachment first, with principal id breaking equal-instant ties.

clauses.subject: registration
clauses.statement: A registration names exactly one form (relative horizon, absolute deadline, open watch) and one source (`metric`, `adjudicator`, `manual`), with a comparator exactly when the source is `metric`; otherwise it raises `OutcomeRegistrationInvalid`.

clauses.subject: source-mismatch
clauses.statement: An observation carrying a verdict whose resolution source is absent or differs from the registration's raises `OutcomeSourceMismatch`.

clauses.subject: settling-citation
clauses.statement: An `adjudicator` or `manual` verdict without an `http` or `https` settling citation raises `OutcomeCitationMissing`; the citation rides the label view.

clauses.subject: grace-window
clauses.statement: The label join keeps an observation from the prediction instant through the deadline plus an inclusive grace of 86400 s.

clauses.subject: calibration-report
clauses.statement: Calibration reports group settled predictions by shape and predicate, and name sample count, Brier score, expected calibration error and the held-out score used by {{read.synthesize.confidence-calibration}}.

clauses.subject: step-output
clauses.statement: A journaled step's value is recorded exactly once and its effect runs at least once: a crash between effect and write re-enters the effect, and every later call under the key returns the recorded value.
clauses.why: because exactly-once effects need the vendor's cooperation, and the recorded value is the one fact a replay can rely on

clauses.subject: entry-key
clauses.statement: An entry is keyed by `(execution_id, step_label, input_hash)`. The first caller claims the key with a pending row before entering the effect; a racing caller waits for the recorded value instead of computing.
clauses.why: because two racers computing one key issue two billed calls and spend two meter permits

clauses.subject: claim-takeover
clauses.statement: A pending claim whose run owner lease has expired, {{run.record.owner-lease}}, is taken over by the next caller under that key.

clauses.subject: idempotency-key
clauses.statement: Every outbound request a step makes carries an idempotency key derived from its entry key, identical on every re-entry of that effect.
clauses.why: because a vendor honoring the key turns an at-least-once effect into one billed call

clauses.subject: inline-cutoff
clauses.statement: A value of 1 MiB or smaller is stored inline in its row as bytes; a larger value lands in a content-addressed blob named by its sha256, and the row holds the reference.

clauses.subject: blob-write
clauses.statement: Concurrent writers of one blob hash converge on one stored value and none errors on another's write; no partial write survives beside it.

clauses.subject: missing-blob
clauses.statement: A row whose blob reference resolves to no stored blob raises `BlobMissing` carrying the reference, never an empty value in place of the recorded one.

clauses.subject: collection
clauses.statement: Retiring an execution owner deletes its journal rows in the retiring transaction.
clauses.why: because recorded work is needed only while a replay can reach it, and an uncollected journal grows with total ingest

clauses.subject: blob-sweep
clauses.statement: A mark-and-sweep pass every 24 h deletes each blob that no journal row or pending awakeable references and that is older than 1 h.
clauses.why: because the grace window covers a blob written ahead of the row that names it

clauses.subject: effect-boundary
clauses.statement: A body replays faithfully when every observable side effect passes through a recorded step, a cursor commit or an awakeable; the work between them is pure.

clauses.subject: recorded-batch
clauses.statement: A journaled pull records the batch as the source handed it over, after {{run.guard-secrets.placement}} and ahead of the land path.

clauses.subject: replay-lands
clauses.statement: A journal hit hands the recorded batch to the land path, so a resumed run lands bytes identical to an uninterrupted one, batch ordinal included.

clauses.subject: ledger-settles-first
clauses.statement: The outbound request ledger settles durably before the entry recording its batch commits.

clauses.subject: redacting-source
clauses.statement: A pipeline declaring write-path redaction over a source that journals its pulls raises `JournalRedactionConflict` at manifest validation and again at run open, before the first pull.

clauses.subject: opt-out
clauses.statement: Pull journaling defaults on. A source whose pre-pull cursor cannot name the content it reads opts out through one constant, pinned against each source's declaration by a test. An empty pull is never journaled.

clauses.subject: escape-hatch
clauses.statement: Two escape hatches exist and no third: `journal.unsafe(label, effect)` for an idempotent read, and a source declaring that it journals no pull. Each carries its idempotency argument at a greppable call site.

clauses.subject: substrate-port
clauses.statement: The run-path substrate is one interface: open or resume an execution under a scope for a content-hashed plan reference, record a step output, commit a cursor, suspend on an awakeable with a timeout, attach a retry schedule, describe capabilities.

clauses.subject: storage-ports
clauses.statement: Journal rows, blobs and awakeables persist through a journal store, a blob store and an awakeable store; every `run.journal` and `run.suspend` clause holds for each adapter, the file tree included.

clauses.subject: sqlite-stores
clauses.statement: `contextful-sqlite` serves the journal, blob and awakeable stores from one SQLite file in write-ahead-log mode over one connection, a blob as a row keyed by its sha256; an awakeable update commits with the journal writes inside it.
clauses.why: because a resolution recording its payload through a second connection waits on the write lock its own update holds

clauses.subject: sqlite-write-lock
clauses.statement: Every `contextful-sqlite` store write opens an immediate transaction, so concurrent writers of one key across connections to one file serialize: one record lands, and every other returns the standing value instead of a locked-database failure.
clauses.why: because under write-ahead logging a deferred read upgrading to a write fails on the lock at once instead of waiting through the busy timeout

clauses.subject: plan-pin
clauses.statement: A run resolves the plan reference it started against for its whole life.

clauses.subject: store-input
clauses.statement: A store-driven run reads its statement once, through the read face under the job's grant at its `as_of`, and records the resolved snapshot id per table and the ordered input rows as its first step.

clauses.subject: input-replay
clauses.statement: A resume iterates the recorded input and never re-reads the statement, so a row landed after the pinned `as_of`, or folded since, never enters the input set.

clauses.subject: open-as-of
clauses.statement: A store-driven job declaring no `as_of` resolves it to the instant its execution opens, recorded in the input step, so every resume reads that instant.

clauses.subject: input-pin
clauses.statement: A store-driven run's plan reference hashes its body name, statement and declared `as_of`, so a resume under a changed one meets {{run.own.pinned-plan-changed}} before any step replays.

clauses.subject: input-truncated
clauses.statement: An input statement whose response the face truncates at its row ceiling raises `RunInputTruncated` before any row runs.
clauses.why: because a silently shortened input set closes `success` as though every row ran

clauses.subject: row-step
clauses.statement: Each input row runs the registered body under a row key, its ordinal in the recorded input; every step the body records carries a label scoped to that key, and a paid call carries {{run.journal.idempotency-key}}.
clauses.why: because two rows sharing one label under one execution resolve to one recorded value

clauses.subject: row-concurrency
clauses.statement: A store-driven run holds at most `max_in_flight` rows inside the body at once; a failing row admits no further row, and the run closes after the rows in flight return.

clauses.subject: row-output
clauses.statement: The rows every body emits land after the last input row completes and before the owner retires, one run per declared output table through {{run.land.stage-order}}.
clauses.why: because a landing that fails then holds the owner, and its resume replays every paid call instead of paying again

clauses.subject: unwired-capability
clauses.statement: Reaching for a capability the running profile does not wire raises `CapabilityUnwired` at the first reach, before any half-finished work.

clauses.subject: machine-state
clauses.statement: Journal rows, execution owners and awakeables live in the host's own stores, never in the derived catalog; a catalog rebuild leaves them untouched and reconstructs none from the file tree.

clauses.subject: cursor-kind
clauses.statement: A cursor declares `monotonic` for a timestamp, autoincrement or watermark, `opaque-token` for a vendor continuation token, or `snapshot-id` for a log sequence number or version id. An undeclared kind resolves to `opaque-token`.

clauses.subject: concurrency-by-kind
clauses.statement: A `monotonic` position is concurrent-safe and commits the highest value observed. An `opaque-token` or `snapshot-id` position moves only under a single-writer lease. Last-write-wins governs no cursor.
clauses.why: because two writers resolving one continuation token by recency skip or duplicate records with no count showing it

clauses.subject: engine-owned
clauses.statement: A connector moves its position only by committing through the engine; that commit is a recorded step and replays as a resolved read.

clauses.subject: commit-with-rows
clauses.statement: A table's new position rides the run commit marker, {{store.lay-out.run-manifest}}, that publishes the rows behind it; the catalog cursor is a cache of the newest committed marker.
clauses.why: because rows and position committed in two stores leave a crash window that re-lands a batch

clauses.subject: cursor-bytes
clauses.statement: A position is opaque bytes the connector owns, and its kind is a manifest fact the engine reads. Each table carries its own position.

clauses.subject: inclusive-boundary
clauses.statement: A polled load admits a row whose clock value is at or after the stored position, re-landing the boundary instant's rows on every poll.
clauses.why: because a clock coarser than the row grain otherwise drops a sibling sharing the boundary value, permanently and invisibly

clauses.subject: declared-key-required
clauses.statement: The boundary re-land is idempotent on a table declaring a key; on a keyless table the repeats accumulate in its union view.

clauses.subject: watermark-shape
clauses.statement: A watermark position serializes as `{"field": "<name>", "at": <value>}`, naming the column it was measured against.

clauses.subject: field-rename
clauses.statement: Opening a position whose stored field differs from the declared `incremental` field raises `CursorFieldMismatch` before any request leaves the host.

clauses.subject: frontier
clauses.statement: The frontier counts every fetched row, landed or not. A committed position moves forward or holds; an empty or older window never rewinds it.

clauses.subject: unorderable-position
clauses.statement: A row with no orderable value in the clock field, or a stream switching between text and numeric positions mid-pass, raises `CursorPositionUnorderable`, terminal for the pull.

clauses.subject: turning-incremental-on
clauses.statement: Enabling `incremental` on a pipeline that holds a position starts from none, re-landing the source's current window once.

clauses.subject: skip-unchanged
clauses.statement: A snapshot-shaped source with `skip_unchanged = true` records its input's raw-byte digest as `{ sha256, rows }`; a matching digest returns zero batches, holds the position and closes a zero-row success. Undeclared, it is false.

clauses.subject: zero-row-commit
clauses.statement: A commit landing zero rows adds and replaces nothing, so a replacing table keeps its last non-empty state across a skip or an empty pull.

clauses.subject: awakeable
clauses.statement: An awakeable suspends a run durably: the engine mints an opaque single-use token and persists a `pending` row through the awakeable store; an external party resumes by posting the token back.

clauses.subject: resume-is-a-step-output
clauses.statement: A resume payload is recorded as the awaited step's output under key `sha256("awakeable:" + token)`, so a run that resumes and then crashes reads it back without suspending again.

clauses.subject: deadline
clauses.statement: A deadline is the creation instant plus a time-to-live, both caller-supplied RFC3339 Zulu strings; the core reads no wall clock.

clauses.subject: timeout-is-sticky
clauses.statement: Expiry is evaluated against an injected instant; a suspension past its deadline becomes `timed_out` and stays so under any later instant.

clauses.subject: idempotent-resolution
clauses.statement: Resolving a token again with the identical payload returns the recorded value.

clauses.subject: conflicting-resolution
clauses.statement: A second resolution with a different payload raises `AwakeableAlreadyResolved` and leaves the recorded value untouched.

clauses.subject: expired-token
clauses.statement: Resolving a token past its deadline raises `AwakeableTimedOut`.

clauses.subject: unknown-token
clauses.statement: A token with no row raises `AwakeableUnknown` and allocates no state.

clauses.subject: resume-route
clauses.statement: `POST /awake/:token` answers `200` with the recorded payload, `404` for {{run.suspend.unknown-token}}, `409` for {{run.suspend.conflicting-resolution}} and `410` for {{run.suspend.expired-token}}. `GET /awake/:token` reports state without resuming. Both authenticate before touching the registry.

clauses.subject: payload-offload
clauses.statement: A payload above {{run.journal.inline-cutoff}} lands in the journal's blob store, and the pending row references it.

clauses.subject: survives-restart
clauses.statement: A durable awakeable store persists every registry row, so a process reopening it over the same location drops no pending callback; an in-process store ends with its process.

clauses.subject: row-parks
clauses.statement: A store-driven row awaiting an unresolved awakeable parks and frees its slot; the other rows run on, and the parked row re-enters its body once the awakeable resolves or its deadline passes.

clauses.subject: recorded-timeout
clauses.statement: A row's wait past its deadline records a timeout value as that wait's step output, so every re-entry of the body reads the identical value.
clauses.why: because a body branching on the clock rather than on a recorded value replays differently after a crash

clauses.subject: failure-taxonomy
clauses.statement: One tagged failure type crosses every port: `Transient`, `Permanent`, `SchemaIncompatible`, `AuthExpired`, `RateLimited`, `Config`, `Storage`, `UnknownConnector`, `SecretNotFound` and `Canceled`. A caller branches on the tag, never on a message.

clauses.subject: schedule
clauses.statement: A schedule attaches to a step and carries a fixed or exponential backoff with base and factor, a total attempt count including the first, a per-delay clamp, a jitter ceiling and `retry_on`.

clauses.subject: default-policy
clauses.statement: The default schedule is exponential from a 100 ms base with factor 2, to 5 attempts in total, each delay clamped at 30 s, plus seeded jitter below 250 ms.
clauses.why: because zero jitter synchronizes every run that hit one shared throttle

clauses.subject: single-attempt
clauses.statement: A schedule of 1 attempts is the no-retry schedule.

clauses.subject: retryable-classes
clauses.statement: `Transient` and `RateLimited` retry; every other tag stands as the step's answer whatever budget remains. `retry_on` narrows that pair.

clauses.subject: unretryable-tag
clauses.statement: A `retry_on` naming any tag outside `Transient` and `RateLimited` raises `RunRetryTagUnretryable` at plan compile.

clauses.subject: step-failed
clauses.statement: A non-retryable failure, or a step exhausting its schedule, raises `StepFailed` carrying the step label and the underlying tag.

clauses.subject: deterministic-verdict
clauses.statement: A refusal whose check is pure over static input is terminal and consumes no attempt budget.

clauses.subject: retry-after
clauses.statement: A server-supplied `Retry-After` supersedes the computed delay up to 300 s; a longer one closes the step as `RateLimited` and the run is rescheduled instead of sleeping.
clauses.why: because an unclamped upstream delay holds a run slot for as long as the vendor asks

clauses.subject: one-layer
clauses.statement: The step's schedule is the only retry layer: an adapter, a credential mint and a meter acquire inside a step return their failure to it.
clauses.why: because nested retry layers multiply attempts and amplify a vendor outage

clauses.subject: decision-is-pure
clauses.statement: The retry decision is a pure function of the one-based attempt that just closed and the classified failure, jitter derived from an injected seed. The runner owns the sleep and the attempt counter.

clauses.subject: partial-failure
clauses.statement: A run that landed some batches and then failed closes `partial_failure`, naming how many landed; the journal holds the resume point.

clauses.subject: pressure-is-local
clauses.statement: Rate-limit pressure against one source paces only that source's runs.

clauses.subject: bound-hit-is-transient
clauses.statement: A connector striking one of its declared resource bounds answers `Transient`, and every bound decision is recorded on the run record.

clauses.subject: execution-owner
clauses.statement: One durable execution owner exists per scope; a table or chunk owner holds the connector identity with its component world, the pipeline `content_hash` and the input hash.

clauses.subject: host-scope
clauses.statement: The catalog keys every owner on its scope — live table, backfill chunk or host-declared id — a table owner keeping its stored key byte for byte, and a host owner pinning the plan reference and identities the host supplies.

clauses.subject: execution-id-keys-the-journal
clauses.statement: Recorded work keys on the execution id; a catalog run id is the provenance of one attempt, so attempts under one owner resolve the same recorded values.

clauses.subject: retirement
clauses.statement: Retiring an owner and caching its committed position share one catalog transaction; a later fire receives a fresh execution id even at a byte-identical position. A completed backfill chunk retires the same way.

clauses.subject: marker-reconciles
clauses.statement: At run open, a commit marker newer than the catalog's cached position retires the pending owner that produced it before any replay.
clauses.why: because a crash between marker and catalog otherwise replays a recorded pull into rows already committed

clauses.subject: pinned-plan-changed
clauses.statement: While an owner is pending, a changed pin — connector identity, component world, pipeline `content_hash`, or a host's plan reference or identities — raises `ExecutionPinMismatch` before replay, terminal and non-retryable, naming the scope and both pin sets.
scenarios: WHEN a host scope's pending owner pins plan reference `plan-a` and an open asks for `plan-b`, THEN the open refuses with `ExecutionPinMismatch` and its run row closes `failed`.

clauses.subject: pin-recovery
