clauses.subject: local-transport
clauses.statement: A local transport is a stdio pipe the checkpoint inherited from the process that spawned it, or a Unix socket; every other transport is a network transport.

clauses.subject: local-holder-proof
clauses.statement: On a local transport, a credential whose confirmation claim holds a thumbprint admits only with a proof as {{authority.verify.possession-binding}}; the peer fallback never applies to it, and a missing or failing proof is refused as {{authority.verify.possession-invalid}}.

clauses.subject: local-proof-channel
clauses.statement: A credentialed command-line verb and the stdio tool server sign one holder proof at admission with the Ed25519 seed in `--holder-key`, else take the proof in `CONTEXTFUL_DPOP`, else sign with the seed in `CONTEXTFUL_HOLDER_KEY`; a blank variable is unset.
clauses.why: because a bound credential is otherwise unusable off the network face, and a proof on the argument list is readable through the process table

clauses.subject: local-proof-request
clauses.statement: A local proof covers method `CLI`, the verb's command path as target, such as `context land`, `memory write` or `mcp`, and an empty body.
clauses.why: because binding the verb keeps a proof minted for a read from admitting a write

clauses.subject: local-nonce-store
clauses.statement: A command-line verb checks its holder proof against the nonce store `.contextful/proof-nonces` under the project root, shared by every invocation on that project under an exclusive lock, so a repeated nonce raises {{authority.verify.replayed-nonce}}.
clauses.why: because each invocation is a fresh process, and a per-process cache lets a proof copied from the environment replay for the whole window

clauses.subject: holder-keygen
clauses.statement: `token keygen --holder` writes an Ed25519 holder seed and prints its thumbprint, the value `token mint --holder` binds as the confirmation claim.

clauses.subject: local-peer-fallback
clauses.statement: On a local transport, a credential with no confirmation claim admits only through the operating system's peer authentication: an inherited stdio pipe, or a socket peer whose kernel-reported uid equals the checkpoint process's uid.

clauses.subject: peer-mismatch
clauses.statement: A socket peer presenting a credential with no confirmation claim, whose kernel-reported uid differs from the checkpoint process's uid or which the platform cannot report, raises `TransportPeerMismatch` and admits nothing.

clauses.subject: network-bearer
clauses.statement: A network checkpoint admits a credential with no confirmation claim as a bearer when it names the checkpoint's declared audience and meets {{authority.verify.bearer-lifetime}}; the peer fallback never applies over a network.

clauses.subject: bearer-lifetime
clauses.statement: A bearer whose expiry falls more than 3600 s after its issue instant raises `BearerLifetimeExceeded` at a network checkpoint and admits nothing; its holder refreshes through {{authority.exchange.surface}}.

clauses.subject: connection-scoped
clauses.statement: A local admission binds to the pipe or socket connection that presented the credential; a request on any other connection is refused as {{authority.verify.peer-mismatch}} until that connection presents the credential and admits itself.

clauses.subject: nonce-cache
clauses.statement: A checkpoint's nonce cache holds at most 100000 entries; a proof arriving while it is full answers `503` and admits nothing.
clauses.why: because a proof the cache cannot record is a replay it cannot detect

clauses.subject: public-key-only
clauses.statement: A checkpoint holds public key material and no signing secret, and admits with no call to an issuer, identity provider or policy service.

clauses.subject: key-set
clauses.statement: A checkpoint accepts a set of issuer keys: comma-separated static pins, or a project-published unauthenticated key route returning the current and non-retired versions, opted into per key.

clauses.subject: pin-source
clauses.statement: A command-line checkpoint reads its pins from `--public-key`, else `CONTEXTFUL_ISSUER_PUBKEY`, and its audience from `--audience`, else `CONTEXTFUL_AUDIENCE`. A bare 64-hex pin reads as `ed25519/<hex>`; an unknown scheme prefix is refused as {{authority.verify.key-set-unavailable}}, naming the accepted forms.
clauses.why: because an operator exports the issuer key once per shell, and key tools commonly print a bare Ed25519 key with no scheme prefix

clauses.subject: key-set-refresh
clauses.statement: A published key set refreshes every 300 s, single-flight, plus one refresh on a signature failure, with failure-forced refreshes throttled.

clauses.subject: key-set-unavailable
clauses.statement: A checkpoint opted into a published key set that obtains none, or holding a malformed pin, raises `KeySetUnavailable`: the engine declines to start and a gateway answers `503`.

clauses.subject: key-set-stale
clauses.statement: After a failed fetch the last-known-good set serves while its age since the last successful fetch stays under 1 h; past that the checkpoint raises `KeySetStale`.

clauses.subject: short-lifetime
clauses.statement: A short lifetime is the primary withdrawal: a credential's remaining lifetime bounds its exposure after a provider sign-out or before a denylist entry propagates.

clauses.subject: denylist
clauses.statement: A checkpoint reads a denylist keyed on credential identifier. An entry ages out once its identifier verifies under no live key version.

clauses.subject: revocation-id
clauses.statement: Every derivation carries its own revocation identifier, withdrawing one subtree without ending the root it descends from.

clauses.subject: epoch
clauses.statement: A revocation epoch scoped on project, tenant and principal class invalidates that slice of outstanding authority.

clauses.subject: epoch-store
clauses.statement: A project persists each scope's current epoch and each issuer key version's retirement in `.contextful/keyset.toml` beside the issuer seed; a mint stamps its scope's current epoch, and a checkpoint re-reads the file at each admission.
clauses.why: because a file the checkpoint reads locally keeps a policy service off the admission path, and the seed's directory already holds the issuer's custody

clauses.subject: ledger-unavailable
clauses.statement: A checkpoint pointed at a key-set ledger, or that has read one, raises `KeySetLedgerUnavailable` and admits nothing once the file is absent or malformed.
clauses.why: because a vanished ledger read as empty lifts every key retirement and epoch bump

clauses.subject: unknown-principal-class
clauses.statement: `contextful token revoke --principal-class` naming neither `delegated` nor `unattributed` raises `RevocationPrincipalClassUnknown` and bumps nothing.
clauses.why: because an epoch under a class no credential carries withdraws nothing while reporting success

clauses.subject: revoked
clauses.statement: A credential on the denylist, or carrying an epoch below the current scoped epoch, raises `AuthorityRevoked` at the next effect boundary.

clauses.subject: compromise
clauses.statement: Suspected compromise of signing material runs a project-wide epoch bump together with immediate retirement of the key version. Waiting out a grace window withdraws nothing.

clauses.subject: rotation-grace
clauses.statement: A rotation policy declares a cadence and a grace window, validated against the persisted issuance policy, during which the retiring key version still verifies.

clauses.subject: short-grace
clauses.statement: A declared or overridden grace window shorter than the effective issuance ceiling raises `RotationGraceTooShort`.

clauses.subject: immediate-retire
clauses.statement: Immediate retirement removes a key version from the published set and every static pin; a checkpoint drops it at its next refresh.

clauses.subject: format-withdrawn
clauses.statement: From a declared cutover instant, every admission path raises `CredentialFormatWithdrawn` for a credential in a withdrawn format. Only an explicit declaration restores acceptance.

clauses.subject: surface
clauses.statement: `contextful token exchange` and `POST /auth/exchange` trade a verified external assertion for a capability credential, configured per project by `.contextful/exchange/policy.toml` and `.contextful/exchange/verify.key`. The command reads the assertion from `--jwt` or standard input, and a holder proof from `--dpop`.

clauses.subject: wire
clauses.statement: An exchange request body is the JSON object `{"jwt": "<assertion>"}`, which the command line builds from its assertion; a body of any other shape raises `ExchangeRequestMalformed` and mints nothing. A served face answers a mint `{"token": "<credential>"}`.
clauses.why: because the command line and every served face parse one body through one function, so a refusal reads the same on both

clauses.subject: body-ceiling
clauses.statement: An exchange request body holds at most 64 KiB; a longer body raises `ExchangeBodyTooLarge`, mints nothing and is not parsed.
clauses.why: because an assertion is a few KiB, and parsing an unbounded body is work an unauthenticated caller spends

clauses.subject: unconfigured
clauses.statement: An exchange in a project declaring no exchange policy raises `ExchangeUnconfigured`, naming `.contextful/exchange/policy.toml`, before the body is read.
clauses.why: because an unconfigured project exposes no exchange, whatever a caller sends

clauses.subject: status-map
clauses.statement: Over HTTP, {{authority.exchange.unconfigured}} answers 404, {{authority.exchange.wire}} and {{authority.exchange.holder-proof-invalid}} 400, {{authority.exchange.body-ceiling}} 413, {{authority.exchange.material-missing}} 503, {{authority.exchange.assertion-invalid}} 401, and any other refusal 403; every refusal body is `{"error": {"http", "identifier", "message"}}`.
clauses.why: because a caller repairs a 400 or 413, retries a 503, re-authenticates on a 401, and repairs nothing on a 403

clauses.subject: signing-fault
clauses.statement: Over HTTP, {{authority.issue.missing-key}}, {{authority.issue.unresolvable-key}}, {{authority.issue.algorithm-mismatch}} or {{authority.issue.replica-mint}} during an exchange answers 500, the body naming the identifier and withholding the refusal's detail.
clauses.why: because the face's operator repairs its configuration, and the detail describes the face's keys to an unauthenticated caller

clauses.subject: policy
clauses.statement: An exchange policy declares `expected_iss`, optional `expected_aud`, `subject_map`, `tenant_claim`, `role_claim`, `role_grants`, `default_grants`, `ttl_secs`, `minted_iss` and `minted_aud`.

clauses.subject: injected-material
clauses.statement: Verifying material is operator-injected: a shared secret, an RS256 public key in PEM form, or a key-set document selected by the assertion's `kid`. The exchange makes no network call.

clauses.subject: minted-grants
clauses.statement: Minted grants come from `role_grants` and `default_grants` alone. A verified role matching no entry earns `default_grants`, which is empty unless declared.

clauses.subject: tenant
clauses.statement: The assertion claim `tenant_claim` names becomes the tenant scope of every minted grant; no subject member carries tenancy.

clauses.subject: lifetime-default
clauses.statement: A minted credential lives 900 s where the policy declares no `ttl_secs`.

clauses.subject: lifetime-ceiling
clauses.statement: A configured `ttl_secs` clamps down to 3600 s and never extends.

clauses.subject: audience
clauses.statement: A minted credential carries `minted_aud`, falling back to the project's persisted default audience.

clauses.subject: assertion-invalid
clauses.statement: A bad signature, a lapsed assertion, an untrusted issuer or audience, or a mapped claim absent from the assertion raises `ExchangeAssertionInvalid` and mints nothing.
clauses.why: because no credential exists whose subject the assertion did not verify

clauses.subject: material-missing
clauses.statement: An exchange configured with no verifying material raises `ExchangeMaterialMissing` and mints nothing.

clauses.subject: per-reader
clauses.statement: An embedding application holds no project-wide credential; per request it exchanges its signed-in reader's assertion for that reader's short-lived credential and reads as them.

clauses.subject: no-cross-reader
clauses.statement: An exchanged credential serves only the reader it was minted for.

clauses.subject: holder-binding
clauses.statement: An exchange request carrying a `DPoP` proof over `POST /auth/exchange` and its body mints a credential whose `cnf.jkt` is the proof key's thumbprint, the proof checked as {{authority.verify.possession-binding}}.

clauses.subject: bearer-mint
clauses.statement: An exchange request carrying no proof mints a credential with no confirmation claim, its lifetime clamped by {{authority.exchange.lifetime-ceiling}}, so a network face admits it under {{authority.verify.bearer-lifetime}}.

clauses.subject: holder-proof-invalid
clauses.statement: An exchange request whose proof fails any check of {{authority.exchange.holder-binding}}, a replayed nonce included, raises `ExchangeHolderProofInvalid` and mints nothing.
clauses.why: because a proof the face cannot verify proves no key, and a bearer minted in its place hands replayable bytes to a caller asking for a bound credential

clauses.subject: refresh
clauses.statement: A holder renews a served-face credential by exchanging a fresh assertion for a new credential with its own identifier and a full lifetime from the exchange instant.

clauses.subject: no-extension
clauses.statement: No surface extends a minted credential's expiry: a minted credential presented as the exchange assertion raises {{authority.exchange.assertion-invalid}}, and {{authority.attenuate.expiry-extended}} bounds every derived child.

clauses.subject: write-time
clauses.statement: Redaction runs inside the writer before columnar encoding. Each rule drops its value or transforms it into a policy-defined substitute: keyed digest, token, prefix or generalized band.

clauses.subject: rule
clauses.statement: A rule names a table, a column, one operation and that operation's argument.

clauses.subject: pipeline-wide
clauses.statement: A rule set declared on a pipeline binds every table the pipeline lands, child tables included.

clauses.subject: after-normalization
clauses.statement: Redaction runs after relational normalization; a rule naming a parent column reaches values shredded into child tables.

clauses.subject: before-the-record
clauses.statement: A removed value is absent from the run path's durable record of the step; {{run.journal.redacting-source}} governs a source journaled verbatim.

clauses.subject: refetch
clauses.statement: Re-running a pipeline over a table under removal rules reads the source again.

clauses.subject: at-rest-scope
clauses.statement: Stored bytes lack only write-time-removed values. A column protected at query time alone is cleartext in storage and readable with the object-store credential.

clauses.subject: summarize-only
clauses.statement: A `summarize_only` column stores its text whole; the flag lands at write time and travels with the column, binding every surface through {{authority.mask.verbatim-quote}}.

clauses.subject: rules-per-pipeline
clauses.statement: A pipeline carries at most 256 entries in its removal rule set.
clauses.why: because a longer rule set is a policy the operator cannot review

clauses.subject: three-layers
clauses.statement: The reference monitor is three layers: write-time removal, the redistribution bound at push, and row-and-column restriction at query time. A request is authorized at each.

clauses.subject: complete-mediation
clauses.statement: Every read of stored rows traverses the layers. A path reaching stored rows outside a registered relation is a defect, never a documented limitation.

clauses.subject: protection-is-a-rewrite
clauses.statement: Protection is a rewrite in the data plane: predicates compiled into the statement, rewritten projections, a per-credential filter at the sync edge, zone floors. Admission decides entry alone.

clauses.subject: registered-relation
clauses.statement: The compiler emits one relation per granted table, bound to the table's bare name for the session's lifetime. Every retrieval arm reads through it.

clauses.subject: relation-order
clauses.statement: A registered relation applies, in order: mirrored permission semi-join, tenant equality, credential predicate, table policy, project default, table zone, then the column projection carrying masks and zone nulls.

clauses.subject: conjunctive-narrowing
clauses.statement: Steps conjoin: a surviving row survives each step alone, and appending a step removes rows and adds none.

clauses.subject: before-the-cut
clauses.statement: Every step, zone exclusion included, completes before a ranked result is cut to its requested size; visible positions carry no trace of a withheld row.

clauses.subject: vector-arm
clauses.statement: A sidecar vector index returns candidate identifiers, which re-join through the registered relation before contributing to a result.

clauses.subject: replica-again
clauses.statement: A caller holding a filtered replica is constrained again per query, the replica's bytes unchanged.

clauses.subject: session-build
clauses.statement: A session builds its relations at admission and rebuilds them when a revocation or a manifest change invalidates a grant it holds.

clauses.subject: relations-per-session
clauses.statement: A session carries at most 1024 entries in its relation set.
clauses.why: because a larger grant set is a mis-scoped credential

clauses.subject: grammar
clauses.statement: A row predicate is the typed boolean subset of SQL in Shapes: column references, comparisons, conjunction, disjunction, negation, membership lists, pattern matching, null tests and declared-safe scalar functions.

clauses.subject: outside-grammar
clauses.statement: Predicates parse at manifest load; a node outside the grammar raises `EnforcePredicateOutsideGrammar`, naming the node.

clauses.subject: subject-relation
clauses.statement: Subject claims reach a predicate as prepared-statement parameters through a session-scoped subject relation. A claim value carrying SQL syntax occupies a parameter slot and reaches no parser.

clauses.subject: exception
clauses.statement: An exception condition is a boolean expression over subject fields in the same grammar, bound the same way.

clauses.subject: override
clauses.statement: A table-policy predicate overriding for a matching subject condition replaces that one predicate; it reaches neither the tenant equality, the mirrored join nor the credential predicate.

clauses.subject: default-deny
clauses.statement: A table reached with no matching grant yields no rows.

clauses.subject: tenant-equality
clauses.statement: A tenant-scoped grant compiles a bound-parameter byte equality on the tenant column, conjoined by the engine; no consumer statement carries it.

clauses.subject: predicate-size
clauses.statement: A declared predicate holds at most 4 KiB of source text.
clauses.why: because a longer predicate is unreviewable policy

clauses.subject: membership-list
clauses.statement: A membership list inside a predicate holds at most 512 entries.
clauses.why: because a longer list belongs in a mirrored table

clauses.subject: column-policy
clauses.statement: A column declares `class` and `strategy`, optionally `combine`, `crowd` and `summarize_only`, under `[pipeline.tables.policy.columns]`. An undeclared column carries no class.

clauses.subject: class-registry
clauses.statement: `class` takes a value from the class registry in Shapes. `phi` marks protected health data; `ssn`, `phone`, `email` and `mrn` are exhaustible, each carrying a registered domain size.

clauses.subject: unknown-class
clauses.statement: A `class` outside the registry raises `EnforceUnknownClass` at manifest check.

clauses.subject: class-reach
clauses.statement: A column's class reaches write-time removal, query-time masking, zone floors and the protections a release applies to a key it joins on.

clauses.subject: strategies
clauses.statement: The strategies are `drop`, `hash` (keyed), `tokenize` (format-preserving), `truncate`, `bucket` and `range`.

clauses.subject: drop
clauses.statement: `drop` nulls the cell, or yields an empty string for a string column.

clauses.subject: one-value
clauses.statement: A column mask is one value whose primary and combine halves are private; it drives both the write-time and query-time layers, and no consumer applies the primary alone.

clauses.subject: digest-alone
clauses.statement: `hash` or `tokenize` standing alone over an exhaustible class raises `EnforceDigestAloneOnExhaustibleClass`.

clauses.subject: high-entropy
clauses.statement: A column of random identifiers or opaque tokens carries `hash` with no combine.

clauses.subject: combine-generalizes
clauses.statement: A `bucket` or `range` combine behind `hash` or `tokenize` raises `EnforceCombineWithoutGeneralization`; `truncate` is the one combine that generalizes a digest.

clauses.subject: hash-width
clauses.statement: `hash` emits 32 chars of hexadecimal.

clauses.subject: token-width
clauses.statement: `tokenize` emits 20 chars.

clauses.subject: cuts-nothing
clauses.statement: A `truncate` combine at or past its primary's output width raises `EnforceTruncationCutsNothing`.

clauses.subject: crowd
clauses.statement: A column's `crowd`, the fewest inputs one masked output covers, is at least 1000 values and defaults to that floor.

clauses.subject: truncation-ceiling
clauses.statement: Behind a keyed digest over an exhaustible class, a `truncate` width above floor(log_b(domain ÷ `crowd`)), b being 16 for `hash` and 36 for `tokenize`, with domain from the class registry, raises `EnforceTruncationTooWide`.

clauses.subject: pepper
clauses.statement: One environment variable supplies the key for `hash` and `tokenize`, read by both layers as one resolved value.

clauses.subject: development-pepper
clauses.statement: Left unset, the pepper resolves to a constant in the source tree and the process emits one signal per run.

clauses.subject: pseudonymous
clauses.statement: `hash` output is an HMAC-SHA-256 under the pepper and is pseudonymous; no surface labels a masked value anonymous.

clauses.subject: native-digest
clauses.statement: Both layers compute the keyed digest natively; the query layer calls a scalar function holding the pepper in process memory, and a value masked at either layer joins the other.

clauses.subject: key-material
clauses.statement: A compiled relation, query plan or session catalog entry carrying pepper-derived key state raises `EnforceKeyMaterialInRelation`.

clauses.subject: subject-exception
clauses.statement: A mask carries exceptions, each a subject condition in the row-predicate grammar bound through the subject relation.

clauses.subject: in-place
clauses.statement: The masked projection substitutes named columns where they stand; the caller receives the column set and order the unmasked statement produces, and `*` expands to it.

clauses.subject: equality
clauses.statement: An equality filter on a `drop` column matches nothing; on a `hash` column it matches equal digests.

clauses.subject: aggregates
clauses.statement: Aggregation reads the masked column.

clauses.subject: summarize-only
clauses.statement: `summarize_only` is a flag, not a strategy: the value stays legible to grounding and citation.

clauses.subject: verbatim-quote
clauses.statement: One citation releases at most 280 chars of a `summarize_only` value verbatim, on every surface.

clauses.subject: typed-strategy
clauses.statement: A binary column masks by `drop` or by `hash` over its bytes, a vector or nested column by `drop` alone over the whole column; another strategy on either raises `EnforceStrategyOutsideType` at manifest load.

clauses.subject: absent-column
clauses.statement: A mask naming a column the table's schema omits raises `EnforceMaskOnAbsentColumn` at manifest load, refusing the whole manifest.
clauses.why: because a skipped declaration serves reads under a policy its author believed covered a column

clauses.subject: masks-per-table
clauses.statement: A table carries at most 128 entries in its column mask set.
clauses.why: because a table beyond it needs a drop, not a mask per column

clauses.subject: scope-denied
clauses.statement: A tenant-scoped credential reading another tenant's rows on a granted table raises `EnforceScopeDenied`, as wire code `scope_denied`, HTTP `403` or an in-band tool error, naming the table and both scopes.

clauses.subject: not-empty
clauses.statement: A scope refusal is a typed error, never an empty result.

clauses.subject: echo
clauses.statement: The requested scope in a refusal echoes the statement's value, never a stored value.

clauses.subject: ungranted-table
clauses.statement: A relation the caller holds no grant on, whether or not a table of that name exists, raises `EnforceUnknownRelation` and is absent from listings and descriptions.

clauses.subject: payload
clauses.statement: A refusal payload carries at most 512 B.

clauses.subject: scope-guard
clauses.statement: The scope guard walks the engine's parse once, deciding literal equalities and membership lists over the tenant column and bound template parameters destined for it.

clauses.subject: top-level
clauses.statement: The guard reads top-level conjuncts of a statement whose own FROM names a scoped table.

clauses.subject: guard-walk
clauses.statement: The guard visits at most 4096 entries of one parse tree.

clauses.subject: undecidable
clauses.statement: A constraint the guard cannot settle composes as an ordinary conjunct; the engine-applied equality isolates.

clauses.subject: drifted-scope
clauses.statement: A tenant value matching no partition reads empty, like a tenant that wrote nothing; the read path repairs no transformed scope value.

clauses.subject: withhold
clauses.statement: A cleared redistribution flag withholds every object of the table at push and omits the table's name from the bucket manifest.

clauses.subject: before-diff
clauses.statement: The exclusion applies before the object diff is computed.

clauses.subject: outranks-grants
clauses.statement: The bound holds against a credential granted everything.

clauses.subject: envelopes
clauses.statement: The bound covers the table's columnar files and each pull's verbatim record.

clauses.subject: root-allowlist
clauses.statement: While any table is withheld, a root-level object ships only when the allowlist in Shapes names it.

clauses.subject: root-not-allowlisted
clauses.statement: A root-level object absent from the allowlist raises `EnforceRootObjectNotAllowlisted` at push.

clauses.subject: left-behind
clauses.statement: Clearing the flag over a table an earlier push uploaded raises `EnforceStaleRedistributedObjects`, naming each object and the remedy, deleting none.

clauses.subject: manifest-is-an-index
clauses.statement: An object stays fetchable by its key after the manifest stops naming it; a manifest authorizes nothing.

clauses.subject: report
clauses.statement: A left-behind report names at most 100 files and states the total found.

clauses.subject: two-checks
clauses.statement: The left-behind check runs before and after the upload loop; the guarantee holds for one bucket under one pushing configuration.

clauses.subject: edge-filter
clauses.statement: A serving edge in front of the bucket filters a materialized replica by the pulling credential's grants.

clauses.subject: zone-string
clauses.statement: A zone string parses, after trimming, as `local:device`, `on-prem:<id>`, `private-cloud:<id>` or `public-cloud:<id>`; any other text is undeclared. The identifier is part of the value.

clauses.subject: allow-set-entry
clauses.statement: An allow-set entry is `*`, `local:device`, `on-prem:*`, `private-cloud:*`, `public-cloud:*`, or a category carrying a concrete identifier.

clauses.subject: unparsed-pattern
clauses.statement: An allow-set entry matching no entry form raises `EnforceZonePatternUnparsed`, naming the entry.
clauses.why: because an unparsed entry matching nothing hides a policy error; a new zone category updates the grammar first

clauses.subject: disjunctive
clauses.statement: A zone is admitted when any entry matches. A bare category matches every identifier in it; an entry carrying an identifier matches that identifier alone.

clauses.subject: undeclared
clauses.statement: Only `*` admits an undeclared zone.

clauses.subject: caller-zone
clauses.statement: The calling process declares its zone per request; the store carries none.

clauses.subject: asserted-zone
clauses.statement: A zone a request asserts stands only where it equals the zone its credential signs; any other assertion raises `EnforceZoneAssertionWidens`, naming both.
clauses.why: because an unsigned argument able to widen placement makes the signed zone decorative

clauses.subject: picks-no-model
clauses.statement: Placement selects no model and dispatches no inference; the engine's one invocation point is an operator-configured endpoint capability for synthesis.

clauses.subject: fail-closed
clauses.statement: A table declaring no zone policy resolves to the fail-closed pair `local:device` and `on-prem:*`, declared and discovered tables alike.

clauses.subject: permissive-default
clauses.statement: A default resolving an unlabeled table to `*` raises `EnforcePermissiveZoneDefault` where more than one principal owns the store.

clauses.subject: protected-floor
clauses.statement: A `phi` column or table carries a floor at the fail-closed pair; a wider declared set resolves down to it at serve time unless the override names that class or column.

clauses.subject: floor-widened
clauses.statement: A manifest widening a protected-class surface past its floor without an override naming that class raises `EnforceProtectedFloorWidened`.

clauses.subject: removal-with-public-cloud
clauses.statement: A surface declaring write-time removal on a column and an allow-set admitting a public cloud raises `EnforceRemovalWithPublicCloud`.

clauses.subject: narrowest-grain
clauses.statement: A column's set narrows its table's; a principal's set narrows both.

clauses.subject: excluded-row
clauses.statement: Where the table's effective set omits the session's zone, the row leaves the result.

clauses.subject: excluded-cell
clauses.statement: A cell whose effective set omits the session's zone arrives null, a mask exception notwithstanding.

clauses.subject: per-principal
clauses.statement: A principal's allow-set pins every row it authors wherever the row lands. A row with no verified author resolves as an undeclared zone.

clauses.subject: evidence-floor
clauses.statement: A synthesized row declaring a set wider than the intersection of its evidence tables' sets raises `EnforceEvidenceFloorExceeded` and resolves to that intersection.

clauses.subject: incognito
clauses.statement: Incognito pins the session to the fail-closed pair, the uncredentialed local owner's reads included.

clauses.subject: incognito-widening
clauses.statement: A session asserting a zone wider than the incognito pin raises `EnforceIncognitoWidening`.

clauses.subject: team-default
clauses.statement: A project declares a default zone, whether users widen it, and whether incognito is on by default.

clauses.subject: serve-outcome
clauses.statement: Serving one row yields a drop flag and the list of zone-masked columns.

clauses.subject: envelope
clauses.statement: A response envelope carries the zone's removals, the asserted zone and the incognito flag in {{read.respond.restriction-block}}, and no removed value.

clauses.subject: excluded-disclosed
clauses.statement: `rows_dropped` counts the rows the zone step removes from the whole relation, every earlier step applied; the caller's statement, filter and requested size never enter it, and no removed value crosses.

clauses.subject: symbolic-inclusion
clauses.statement: Inclusion against a floor is decided over every constructor and identifier, never by probing sample zones.

clauses.subject: proxy-boundary
clauses.statement: A proxy replica resolves zones at the proxy boundary.

clauses.subject: allow-set-entries
clauses.statement: An allow-set holds at most 32 entries.

clauses.subject: identifier-length
clauses.statement: A zone identifier holds at most 128 chars.

clauses.subject: credential-shaped-value
clauses.statement: The write path raises `EnforceCredentialShapedValue` on a value matching a credential shape, before it reaches storage.

clauses.subject: read-only-face
clauses.statement: An organization-wide face serves the read subset of the tool surface; conversational writes are server-authored.

clauses.subject: write-tool
clauses.statement: Registering a write tool on an organization-wide face raises `EnforceWriteOnReadOnlyFace`.

clauses.subject: unbound-table
clauses.statement: On an organization-wide face, a table with no visibility block raises `VisibilityUnboundTable` from diagnose and from the serving guardrail at start, naming the table.

clauses.subject: incomplete-binding
clauses.statement: A binding at a servable level lacking a declared sweep for its source or a `max_acl_staleness` raises `VisibilityBindingIncomplete`.

clauses.subject: binding-keys
clauses.statement: A table's `visibility` block names its `source`, the `resource_key` column holding each row's `resource_id`, its `resource_kind`, `fidelity`, `family`, `max_acl_staleness`, and `on_stale` of `refuse`, the default, or `public_only`.

clauses.subject: grants-table
clauses.statement: A sweep lands a source's access data as ordinary rows of `_visibility/<source>/resources`, `grants`, `principals`, `group_members`, `identity_links`, `tombstones` and `freshness`, through the land path and its write lock.

clauses.subject: unmirrorable-opening
clauses.statement: A resource whose access list the sweep could not mirror opens only through a grant row the store owner lands carrying `expires_at`; the row confers nothing past that instant, and no manifest key opens a resource.

clauses.subject: coverage-watermark
clauses.statement: A sweep run that failed or skipped any governed resource of its source and advances `watermark_at` raises `VisibilityWatermarkUncovered`, and the watermark stays where it stood.

clauses.subject: ungapped-stream
clauses.statement: Advancing `watermark_at` from an event stream the mapping has not declared gap-detectable raises `VisibilityUngappedStream`.

clauses.subject: orphan-grant
clauses.statement: A grant landing with no resource row, or on a resource of the unknown class, raises `VisibilityOrphanGrant` at commit and joins no reachable set.

clauses.subject: sweep-block
clauses.statement: An `[[acl_sweep]]` block declares one source's sweep: `source`, the `enumerate` table whose rows are its governed resources, `full` and `incremental` cadences as `{ every = <budget> }`, and optional `credential` and `events`.

clauses.subject: cadence-grammar
clauses.statement: A sweep cadence's `every` takes the grammar of {{disclosure.bound-staleness.budget-grammar}}.

clauses.subject: sweep-verb
clauses.statement: `visibility sweep --source <s> --kind full|incremental [--grants <file>]` runs one sweep of a declared source, reading its permission endpoint under `credential`, or the file when `--grants` is given, and commits as one run.

clauses.subject: grants-file
clauses.statement: A `--grants` file is the run's read of every resource `enumerate` names: one JSON object per line with `resource_id`, `principal`, `principal_kind` and `level`; a resource with no line holds no grant.

clauses.subject: full-run
clauses.statement: A full run replaces the source's resource and grant rows with those it read, writes a tombstone per grant it no longer observes, and sets `last_full_sweep_at`.

clauses.subject: incremental-run
clauses.statement: An incremental run replaces the grants of each resource it read, tombstoning those withdrawn, leaves every other resource's grants standing, and sets `last_incremental_at`.

clauses.subject: watermark-advance
clauses.statement: A run reading every governed resource sets the source's `watermark_at` to the instant it began reading; lag is now minus `watermark_at`.

clauses.subject: sweep-epoch
clauses.statement: A committed run advances its source's epoch by one.

clauses.subject: subject-principals
clauses.statement:
A subject `user://

` reaches the `user` principal spelled `

` and each principal an `identity_links` row maps to it, then the groups those principals belong to.

clauses.subject: closure-walk
clauses.statement: The closure walks the group graph with a visited set, ending any cycle, to a depth of `max_group_depth`, default 8 hops, and a breadth of 10000 nodes.

clauses.subject: closure-overflow
clauses.statement: A closure reaching its depth or node bound raises `VisibilityClosureDepth` with the non-retryable HTTP status 422 and returns no set.

clauses.subject: cache-capacity
clauses.statement: The reachable-set cache holds at most 100000 entries and evicts the least recently used.

clauses.subject: degraded-uncached
clauses.statement: Retaining a reachable set or result produced past a budget, or under the narrowing posture, raises `VisibilityDegradedCached`.

clauses.subject: semi-join
clauses.statement: The semi-join opening {{authority.compose.relation-order}} admits a row of a bound table when its `resource_key` value names a resource with a read-conferring, unexpired, untombstoned grant in the reader's reachable set.

clauses.subject: closure-projection
clauses.statement: The group closure is a projection in `derived.sqlite`, rebuilt from the `_visibility` rows after each sweep and on a replica after each pull; no replica opens closure files.

clauses.subject: cache-epochs
clauses.statement: The reachable-set cache keys on the subject, the directory epoch and the epoch of each source the read touches, so a sweep invalidates only sets reading its source.

clauses.subject: budget-grammar
clauses.statement: `max_acl_staleness` is a positive integer with one suffix from `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`. A compound form, a bare number or another suffix raises `VisibilityBudgetMalformed`, naming the table and the text read.

clauses.subject: access-stale
clauses.statement: A read raises `VisibilityAccessStale` (HTTP 503, carrying source, lag, budget and last observation) when a touched table's source lag exceeds its budget, the source has no completed full run, or the public-status watermark is past budget.

clauses.subject: budget-below-cadence
clauses.statement: A budget tighter than the sweep cadence its source sustains raises `VisibilityBudgetUnreachable` at diagnose, naming both figures.

clauses.subject: clock-offset
clauses.statement: `CONTEXTFUL_NOW_OFFSET_SECS`, a non-negative integer, moves the instant a staleness check reads as now that many seconds later, so it can refuse a read and never extends a budget.
clauses.why: because a test observes a budget elapse without waiting, and an offset that only ages state cannot admit a read

clauses.subject: offset-malformed
clauses.statement: A `CONTEXTFUL_NOW_OFFSET_SECS` value other than a non-negative integer stops the process before it serves, naming the variable.

clauses.subject: family-bound
clauses.statement: A `person-container` table at a servable level, or a `directory` table above `excluded`, raises `VisibilityFamilyBound`, and the manifest declaring it does not load.

clauses.subject: family-undeclared
clauses.statement: A mapping landing a table without naming its `family` raises `VisibilityFamilyUndeclared`.

clauses.subject: federated-registered
clauses.statement: Registering a `federated` table on a read face raises `VisibilityFederatedRegistered`.

clauses.subject: federated-cache
clauses.statement: Retaining a federated result under a key omitting the subject raises `VisibilityFederatedCacheShared`.

clauses.subject: computed-inputs
clauses.statement: A source that computes access with a sharing engine is queried live. A mapping projecting that engine's inputs into the `grants` table raises `VisibilityComputedInputsMirrored`, naming the source.

clauses.subject: roster-from-payload
clauses.statement: A mapping deriving grants from a people list inside content — attendees, invitees, recipients, contacts — rather than from the source's permission endpoint raises `VisibilityRosterFromPayload`.

clauses.subject: federated-credential
clauses.statement: A federated leg runs under a credential the read obtains by token exchange for the reader's subject, never under the sweep's `credential` or the store owner's.

clauses.subject: federated-citation
clauses.statement: A federated result with no store row cites the source URL it fetched and the instant of that fetch.

clauses.subject: mapping-absent
clauses.statement: A pack landing a table with neither an access mapping nor `excluded` raises `VisibilityMappingAbsent` at diagnose, naming the pack and the table.

clauses.subject: asserts-access
clauses.statement: An access-shaped key the mapping schema does not define raises `VisibilityPackAssertsAccess` by name. Fields outside the mapping are fetch inputs and reach no authorization decision.

clauses.subject: any-of-allowlist
clauses.statement: An allowlist evaluated as any-of raises `VisibilityAllowlistAnyOf` at load.

clauses.subject: unsupported-coarse
clauses.statement: Declaring `coarse` where the source emits no container or workspace signal raises `VisibilityUnsupportedCoarse`.

clauses.subject: offline-diagnostic
clauses.statement: The single-operator diagnostic reads the manifest and each published model's statement text from local disk and issues 0 requests to the object store.

clauses.subject: policy-absent
clauses.statement: A published aggregate-shaped model carrying neither a disclosure policy nor a recorded opt-out fails the diagnostic with `DisclosurePolicyAbsent`.

clauses.subject: model-unreadable
clauses.statement: A published model whose referenced statement text does not read raises `DisclosureModelUnreadable`.

clauses.subject: clean-room-preconditions
clauses.statement: A cross-owner store carries per-owner signed manifest subtrees, per-owner write prefixes enforced by the object store's access policy, and per-owner signing keys; one missing, checked before any cross-prefix write, raises `DisclosureCleanRoomPreconditionUnmet`.

clauses.subject: hashed-join
clauses.statement: Two owners match on a key each hashes at write time under a per-pair pepper re-randomized per join; matched rows leave as an aggregate under a group-size floor. A static pepper raises `DisclosureStaticPepper`.

clauses.subject: budget-reservation
clauses.statement: Before computing, a release reserves each contributing unit's declared per-run spend against its lifetime cap in one catalog transaction. A failed reservation raises `DisclosureUnitBudgetExhausted`, and the release publishes nothing.

clauses.subject: duplicate-grain
clauses.statement: A non-numeric, non-grain column rides the grouping, and one not constant within its group raises `DisclosureDuplicateGrain`.

clauses.subject: group-key
clauses.statement: A group key not a subset of the permitted grouping columns raises `DisclosureGroupKeyNotPermitted`.

clauses.subject: contributor-key
clauses.statement: A governed statement omitting the contributor key raises `DisclosureContributorKeyAbsent`.

clauses.subject: forbidden-column
clauses.statement: A contract declaring a forbidden column, or a materialization producing one, raises `DisclosureForbiddenColumnPublished`. The check runs after the contributor key leaves the published columns.

clauses.subject: min-group-size
clauses.statement: `min_group_size` counts distinct contributors and is at least 2 subjects. A group whose noised distinct-contributor count falls under it is suppressed, and a smaller declared value raises `DisclosureMinGroupSizeBelowFloor`.

clauses.subject: contributor-share
clauses.statement: `max_contributor_share` lies above 0 percent and at most 100 percent of a group's sign-insensitive metric mass; a value outside raises `DisclosureShareOutOfRange`.

clauses.subject: dominance-unverifiable
clauses.statement: A group under a share constraint whose per-contributor masses are unavailable raises `DisclosureDominanceUnverifiable` and is suppressed.

clauses.subject: empty-policy
clauses.statement: A policy setting neither threshold, or only a share ceiling at a whole group's mass, raises `DisclosurePolicySuppressesNothing`.

clauses.subject: grouping-allowlist
clauses.statement: An empty permitted-grouping list, or a permitted name that is not column-shaped, raises `DisclosureGroupingAllowlistEmpty`.

clauses.subject: single-statement
clauses.statement: A declaration holding more than one statement raises `DisclosureTemplateMultiStatement`.

clauses.subject: overfetch
clauses.statement: A capped result sets the envelope's truncation flag by reading exactly 1 rows past the effective ceiling.

clauses.subject: cohort-widening
clauses.statement: A read recovering an under-floor group by merging it into a coarser key raises `DisclosureCohortWidening`.

clauses.subject: per-individual-row
clauses.statement: Reading a per-individual row from a cohort table without an explicit grant on the reader's token raises `DisclosurePerIndividualUngranted`.

clauses.subject: singleton-cohort
clauses.statement: A cohort key whose grain resolves to one person raises `DisclosureSingletonCohort` at declaration, before any row lands under it.

clauses.subject: exact-figures
clauses.statement: A policy declaring `figures = "exact"` on a `per-person` table raises `DisclosureExactPerPerson`. `figures` defaults to `"noised"`, and exact figures publish only from a `cohort` table.

clauses.subject: segment
clauses.statement: Entries append to a numbered segment file in ascending `seq`, and a segment closes under one signed root once it holds its chain header's segment size, 4096 entries by default.

clauses.subject: chain-header
clauses.statement: `header.json`, written before a new chain's first entry, fixes the chain's format, its digest, `sha256` or `blake3`, and a segment size of at most 65536 entries; the first v1 entry's `prev_hash` is the canonical header's digest.

clauses.subject: header-unsupported
clauses.statement: Opening or verifying a chain whose header names another format or digest, a segment size outside {{disclosure.record.chain-header}}, or any field beyond `format`, `digest` and `segment_entries` raises `AuditHeaderUnsupported`.
clauses.why: because a verifier guessing at a digest it does not implement checks nothing

clauses.subject: entry-format
clauses.statement: A v1 entry carries `format: 1`, and its `entry_hash` is the chain header's digest over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the entry's `format`, `seq`, `prev_hash` and `attributes`.

clauses.subject: entry-fields
clauses.statement: Verifying a chain holding an entry with any field beyond `format`, `seq`, `prev_hash`, `attributes` and `entry_hash` raises {{disclosure.attest.broken-chain}} at that entry.
clauses.why: because the entry digest covers only `format`, `seq`, `prev_hash` and `attributes`, so without this an injected field verifies clean

clauses.subject: inexact-integer
clauses.statement: Appending a v1 entry whose attributes hold an integer beyond ±(2^53 − 1) raises `AuditAttributeInexact` and appends nothing; verifying a chain holding such an entry raises {{disclosure.attest.broken-chain}}.
clauses.why: because RFC 8785 writes every number as an IEEE 754 double, so integers past 2^53 share a digest and an edit between two of them verifies

clauses.subject: v0-chain
clauses.statement: A chain holding entries without `header.json` is a v0 chain: it verifies and appends under v0 rules, each entry digest over `seq`, `prev_hash` and attributes and each root its segment's last entry digest.

clauses.subject: group-commit
clauses.statement: Concurrent appends form one append group, which issues 1 sync of its segment file between segment opens; every member returns after that sync, or every member raises {{disclosure.record.unpersisted-entry}}.

clauses.subject: segment-open
clauses.statement: An append group that creates a segment file adds 1 sync of the segments directory.

clauses.subject: tip-signing
clauses.statement: The signed tip writes at segment close, once the log sees no append for 1 s, and at export; an append group closing no segment writes no tip.

clauses.subject: unpersisted-entry
clauses.statement: A read whose entry fails to reach local durable storage raises `AuditEntryUnpersisted` and returns no rows.

clauses.subject: unpersisted-wire
clauses.statement: The read face answers {{disclosure.record.unpersisted-entry}} in-band as wire code `audit_entry_unpersisted`, HTTP `503`, with no `rows` in the result.
clauses.why: because a storage fault is the server's and passes, so a client retries it rather than rewording the read

clauses.subject: read-entry
clauses.statement: Each read tool call the face answers with a result, over stdio or HTTP, appends one entry, and the result leaves only after that entry's append group syncs; `initialize`, `ping` and `tools/list` append none.

clauses.subject: read-attributes
clauses.statement: A read's entry carries `contextful.tool`, `contextful.credential`, `contextful.subject.<member>` and `contextful.subject.attestation.<member>` per present subject member, `contextful.result.rows`, `contextful.read.at`, `contextful.read.outcome` and `contextful.tables`, the relations the read names.
clauses.why: because the chain answers who read how much under which credential, and the attestation keeps an asserted member from reading as identity

clauses.subject: read-chain
clauses.statement: `contextful serve` and `contextful mcp` open the project's chain at `.contextful/audit/` unanchored before answering a message; a chain that does not open stops the process before it reads a row.

clauses.subject: single-writer
clauses.statement: One append group holds a directory's audit log at a time: it takes `audit.lock`, links after the chain end, syncs, then releases the lock, so several processes append to one linear chain.

clauses.subject: foreign-tail
clauses.statement: An append group finding the last segment file changed since its handle's last write reads that segment's last entry before linking, and issues no sync beyond {{disclosure.record.group-commit}}.

clauses.subject: read-only
clauses.statement: A read-only audit handle verifies the chain without the writer lock; an append through it raises `AuditLogReadOnly`.

clauses.subject: unanchored-over-signed
clauses.statement: An unanchored handle links entries under an unsigned tip and writes no root; opening one over a signed tip, a signed root or the signed `chain.held` a held open writes raises `AuditLogAnchored`.

clauses.subject: held-under-append
clauses.statement: An unanchored handle's append group or tip write finding `chain.held` written since its open raises {{disclosure.record.unanchored-over-signed}} and writes nothing, so a held open never meets an unsigned tip or an unrooted segment.
clauses.why: because the lock is held per append group, so a held open can land between two groups of a running unanchored handle

clauses.subject: unsigned-tip
clauses.statement: A held open or signed check over a chain carrying no `chain.held` or signed root, whose tip is unsigned, raises `AuditLogUnanchored`; anchoring through the signing port signs that chain's missing roots and its tip.

clauses.subject: reads-view
clauses.statement: `audit query` runs one statement over `audit_reads`, one row per table a read entry names — `read_at`, `on_behalf_of`, `agent`, `table_name`, `policy`, `outcome`, `row_count` — computed from the chain's segments on each call.

clauses.subject: refused-read
clauses.statement: A read enforcement refuses appends one entry with `outcome` `refused`, naming the relations the guard parsed, and releases no rows.

clauses.subject: projection
clauses.statement: The projection answers which agent read which table under which policy across a rolling 24 h window, within 1 s.

clauses.subject: decision
clauses.statement: `audit explain --table <t> --subject <principal>` answers `admit` when a grant the exchange policy issues for the `--role` names, else its `default_grants`, carries `read` over a pattern covering the table, and `deny` otherwise.

clauses.subject: path
clauses.statement: A decision's path names the role or default set, the covering grant, then each step the table declares in {{authority.compose.relation-order}}; a deny's path ends at {{authority.filter-rows.default-deny}}.

clauses.subject: replay
clauses.statement: `--window <from>..<to>` replays each chain entry naming the subject and the table whose read instant falls in the window: its seq, instant, outcome, agent and recorded `contextful.*` attributes.

clauses.subject: coverage
clauses.statement: An explanation carries a coverage block: segments and entries verified, entries carrying no read instant, window spans the chain does not reach, and each visibility binding's source with its sweep watermark.

clauses.subject: audience
clauses.statement: `audit explain --audience <t>` lists by name the roles whose grants read the table, whether `default_grants` do, and per `on_behalf_of` scheme the count of principals and served reads.

clauses.subject: no-row
clauses.statement: An explanation returning a row, field value or excerpt from the resource it decides about, a replayed `contextful.result.*` attribute beyond `contextful.result.rows` included, raises `VisibilityDiagnosticRow`.

clauses.subject: empty-window
clauses.statement: A window holding no observations raises `VisibilityNoObservations` and states that no claim is available.

clauses.subject: unqualified-assurance
clauses.statement: A negative assurance answer emitted without its coverage block raises `VisibilityUnqualifiedAssurance`.

clauses.subject: groups-not-members
clauses.statement: A reader-facing explanation rendering the member identities of a group on the path raises `VisibilityIndividualNamed`.

clauses.subject: broken-chain
clauses.statement: A disagreeing digest, entry format or Merkle root, a sequence gap, a failing signature, or, beside `chain.tip`, `chain.held` or a signed root, an absent chain or a missing or unsigned tip raises `AuditChainBroken` at the earliest failing index.

clauses.subject: merkle-root
clauses.statement: A v1 segment root is the RFC 6962 Merkle tree hash, under the header's digest, over the segment's raw entry digests in `seq` order.

clauses.subject: root-tag
clauses.statement: A v1 signed root carries its signing algorithm, `Ed25519` or `ES256`, and signs it with the header digest, segment number, entry count and root.

clauses.subject: inclusion-proof
clauses.statement: `prove` returns one entry, its chain header, its RFC 6962 audit path and its segment's signed root; the proof verifies offline under the signer's public key alone.

clauses.subject: proof-invalid
clauses.statement: A proof whose entry, audit path, header, root or root signature disagrees raises `AuditProofInvalid`.

clauses.subject: proof-unavailable
clauses.statement: Proving an entry of a v0 chain, of a segment carrying no signed root, or outside the chain raises `AuditProofUnavailable`.
clauses.why: because an open segment has no signed root yet, and a v0 root commits to no tree

clauses.subject: root-replication
clauses.statement: `audit anchor` once it signs, and a held chain's replicator at start and every 10 min, copy each signed root the `[sync]` bucket lacks to `<prefix>/<project>/audit/roots/<segment>.json`; a failed copy waits for the next and fails no anchor, append or read.

clauses.subject: replica-verify
clauses.statement: `audit verify --bucket` also holds the chain to each replicated root: a root failing its signature, closing a segment the chain does not reach, or absent or different locally breaks the chain as {{disclosure.attest.broken-chain}} does.
clauses.why: because deleting the roots, `chain.held` and the tip's signature leaves a chain no local check tells from an unanchored one

clauses.subject: replicate-verb
clauses.statement: `audit replicate` copies the roots {{disclosure.attest.root-replication}} copies, once, and prints the segments it sent.

clauses.subject: lineage-elision
clauses.statement: A lineage attestation counts a claim's evidence references into tables the caller's session does not register as `withheld` in the `contextful.recall` block, and names no such table.

clauses.subject: verify-verb
clauses.statement: `audit verify` opens the chain read-only and prints its end when every check of {{disclosure.attest.broken-chain}} passes, each signature included under `--public-key`.

clauses.subject: anchor-verb
clauses.statement: `audit anchor --issuer-key <seed>` signs the chain's missing roots and its tip as {{disclosure.record.unsigned-tip}} anchors them, and prints the chain end.

clauses.subject: prove-verb
clauses.statement: `audit prove --seq <n>` prints the proof {{disclosure.attest.inclusion-proof}} returns, and `audit check-proof` verifies one under a public key, reading no store.

clauses.subject: owner-only
clauses.statement: An audit verb reading a chain, presented with a capability credential, raises `AuditRequiresOwner` before it reads an audit file.
clauses.why: because the chain names every person's reads, and a credential scoped to some tables reaches no record of others

clauses.subject: privilege
clauses.statement: Erasure sits outside the default grant set, and a caller without the forget grant raises `ErasureUngranted`.

clauses.subject: subject-column
clauses.statement: A table names its subject column as `subject_id = "<column>"` under `[[pipeline.tables]]`. A subject erasure against a table without one raises `ErasureSubjectUndeclared`, naming the table.

clauses.subject: cascade
clauses.statement: In the same operation the cascade invalidates every derived fact whose provenance reaches the subject key or a tombstoned identifier within 16 hops.

clauses.subject: cascade-unbounded
clauses.statement: A provenance chain deeper than the cascade bound raises `ErasureCascadeUnbounded`, and the erasure commits nothing.

clauses.subject: physical-removal
clauses.statement: Every file holding an erased row, a superseded snapshot still inside {{store.fold.retention}} included, is rewritten or collected within 24 h of the erasure's commit.

clauses.subject: restaging-gate
clauses.statement: `--fail-closed` writes a row-free `{subject_hash, executed_at}` marker at the store root after the cascade. While it stands, every fact read raises `ErasureRestagingRequired`, naming the owed re-synthesis and the clearing verb.

clauses.subject: tenant-column-type
clauses.statement: A tenant column of a non-string type raises `PurgeTenantColumnType`.

clauses.subject: tenant-undeclared
clauses.statement: A purge finding no model declaring an outermost partition key raises `PurgeTenantUndeclared`.

clauses.subject: owner-only
clauses.statement: A purge presented with a capability token raises `PurgeRequiresOwner`, evaluated before anything reveals store contents.

clauses.subject: pseudonym
clauses.statement: `tenant_hash` is SHA-256 over a random per-receipt `salt` and the tenant identifier. A receipt carrying the identifier in cleartext raises `ReceiptIdentifierLeak` before signing.

clauses.subject: widened-claim
clauses.statement: A coverage block naming a scope broader than its `receipt_version` declares raises `ReceiptClaimWidened`.

clauses.subject: replayed
clauses.statement: Returning the byte-identical earlier artifact in place of a freshly signed one raises `ReceiptReplayed`.

clauses.subject: no-rewrite-engine
clauses.statement: A purge where the columnar rewrite engine is unavailable raises `ReceiptWithoutRewrite` and signs nothing.
clauses.why: because a receipt over a rewrite that did not run states a false claim

clauses.subject: unreadable-schedule
clauses.statement: A schedule string the grammar cannot read, including `L`, `W`, `?`, `#` and `@` macros, raises `ScheduleUnreadable` for that entry alone, naming the diagnostic; every other entry of the document arms.

clauses.subject: unknown-trigger
clauses.statement: An unrecognized trigger value raises `TriggerAdapterUnknown` at startup and downgrades onto no adapter.

clauses.subject: trigger-face-missing
clauses.statement: `external` selected on a deployment serving no HTTP face raises `TriggerFaceMissing` at startup.

clauses.subject: wake-answer
clauses.statement: A wake answers within 25 s with what fired, what failed, what stays armed and the next due instant, naming each fire still in flight as pending.
clauses.why: because a platform request timeout otherwise ends the call before the caller learns anything

clauses.subject: tick-interval
clauses.statement: The in-process adapter evaluates the armed set every 500 ms.

clauses.subject: trigger-select
clauses.statement: `[control] trigger` selects `in-process`, the default, or `external`, under which `pipeline serve --http <address>` answers `POST /wake` and runs no tick of its own.

clauses.subject: grammar
clauses.statement: A schedule is `every <n><unit>` with unit `s`, `m`, `h` or `d`, or a UTC cron expression of five fields, minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week, each `*`, a value, range, list or `/` step.

clauses.subject: next-fire-from-history
clauses.statement: An armed entry's next fire is the first instant its schedule admits after the later of its pipeline's last journaled run start and its last dispatch; an entry with neither is due when armed.
clauses.why: because a restarted daemon then keeps the cadence its run history shows instead of restarting every interval from boot

clauses.subject: catch-up
clauses.statement: A daemon arming an entry whose next fire has passed fires it once, whatever count of intervals elapsed, and arms the following fire from that run.
clauses.why: because replaying each missed interval against an incremental source pulls the same delta once per interval

clauses.subject: pulled-history
clauses.statement: A pipeline's last journaled run start is the latest start across this node's catalog and every run state {{store.push.run-state}} carries that records the pipeline.
clauses.why: because a cold node's empty catalog otherwise finds every scheduled entry due at once

clauses.subject: pulled-future
clauses.statement: A pulled run start later than the scheduler's current instant counts as no start for {{surface.arm.pulled-history}}.
clauses.why: because one node's fast clock or one bucket writer otherwise defers every replica's cadence until that instant

clauses.subject: unarmed-named
clauses.statement: An applied pipeline declaring no schedule, or held back by {{surface.arm.unreadable-schedule}}, arms no entry; serve names each such pipeline with its reason once per applied version, and `--cycle` lists them under `unarmed`.
clauses.why: because a pipeline silently left out of the armed set reads as armed until its data goes stale

clauses.subject: poll-cadence
clauses.statement: `poll` takes a schedule string, and a `[control]` block declaring none polls every 30 s.

clauses.subject: pointer-malformed
clauses.statement: A pointer body that is not wholly a version raises `ControlPointerMalformed`.
clauses.why: because an integer read out of leading bytes arms a version nobody applied

clauses.subject: fail-static
clauses.statement: An unreadable pointer, an unparseable snapshot or a control plane answering `5xx` raises `ControlSnapshotUnreadable`, logs a diagnostic, and leaves the armed set in place running.

clauses.subject: loopback-only
clauses.statement: A control URL whose host is not a loopback address raises `ControlSourceNotLoopback` and arms nothing; a poll follows no redirect and routes through no proxy.

clauses.subject: url-layout
clauses.statement: A control URL serves `manifest@current` and each `manifest@v<N>.toml` directly beneath its path; a pointer answered `404` reads as no applied version, and any other status besides `200` is unreadable.
clauses.why: because one layout serves a snapshot directory unchanged over loopback HTTP

clauses.subject: learns-by-reading
clauses.statement: A daemon learns of a new snapshot only by reading its control source, on each poll and on each wake; nothing pushes a snapshot to it.

clauses.subject: job-kind-unknown
clauses.statement: A block naming a kind outside the union, an argument vector or a host command raises `JobKindUnknown` at validation.

clauses.subject: target-unbound
clauses.statement: A `fold` target naming no produced table, or a `build` target naming no produced table declaring its `columns`, raises `JobTargetUnbound` at validation.

clauses.subject: cycle-control-source
clauses.statement: A configured control source that does not resolve under `cycle` raises `CycleControlSourceUnresolved`.

clauses.subject: store-driven-concurrency
clauses.statement: A `store-driven` block declaring no positive integer `max_in_flight` raises `JobConcurrencyUnset` at validation; no default applies.

clauses.subject: store-driven-body
clauses.statement: A `store-driven` block whose `body` names no body the embedding binary registers raises `JobBodyUnregistered` at validation.

clauses.subject: cycle
clauses.statement: `serve --cycle` arms the applied snapshot, evaluates due-ness once, waits for every unit it dispatched, and prints what fired, what failed, what stays pending, the armed count and the next due instant.

clauses.subject: cycle-exit
clauses.statement: `serve --cycle` exits non-zero when any unit it dispatched failed, after printing its answer; a cycle with no failed unit, or one finding the cadence lease held, exits zero.
clauses.why: because a scheduler running the cycle reads the exit status, and a zero over a failed fire reports success

clauses.subject: not-a-head
clauses.statement: A `[[pipeline]]` block naming `after = "<id>"` is a landing step of that entry's dependent run; the run is the unit and cadence rides its head entry. A due id that is a step raises `DispatchUnitNotAHead` and starts nothing.

clauses.subject: step-result
clauses.statement: A completion callback carries a pointer, an object-store key or a catalog row id, or the failed step's last error line, as JSON of at most 1 MiB; any other callback body raises `StepResultRefused` and records nothing.
clauses.why: because a step result rides one journal row, and bulk output belongs in the object store it points into

clauses.subject: in-band-tool-error
clauses.statement: A step driving the engine over the tool protocol judges the tool result, not transport status: a `200` carrying a protocol error or a result flagged `isError` raises `StepToolError`.

clauses.subject: callback-skew
clauses.statement: The relay accepts a callback timestamp within 300 s of its own clock.

clauses.subject: callback-rejected
clauses.statement: A heartbeat or callback whose signature fails, whose attempt is not the step's current attempt, whose timestamp falls outside {{surface.dispatch.callback-skew}}, or whose step has closed, raises `DispatchCallbackRejected` and changes no step.
clauses.why: because a partitioned worker's late result otherwise overwrites its successor's, and a captured callback replays indefinitely

clauses.subject: heartbeat-beat
clauses.statement: A worker heartbeats every 15 s with a signed `GET` on its step's awakeable route, and posts its outcome to that route with a signed `POST`.

clauses.subject: worker-target
clauses.statement: `[control] workers` lists worker URLs and `[control] relay` the URL whose `/awake/:token` route `serve` binds; with workers listed, each landing step posts to a worker's `POST /submit`, keyed by run, step and attempt.

clauses.subject: worker-key
clauses.statement: Heartbeats and callbacks sign under the key `CONTEXTFUL_WORKER_KEY` holds; `serve` listing workers without a relay or without that key refuses at startup and binds nothing.

clauses.subject: submit-signed
clauses.statement: A worker admits a `POST /submit` only when it carries an HMAC under the worker key over its timestamp and body, within {{surface.dispatch.callback-skew}}, naming a callback under its own `[control] relay`; any other submission raises `DispatchSubmitRejected` and starts nothing.
clauses.why: because an unsigned submission lets any caller start a step and have the worker sign heartbeats and callbacks for a route of its choosing

clauses.subject: submit-exhausted
clauses.statement: A step every listed worker refuses in turn at `POST /submit` fails its unit naming the last refusal, each worker tried once.
clauses.why: because a step bouncing between refusing workers holds its pool slot and exclusion key while never running

clauses.subject: heartbeat-lapse
clauses.statement: A heartbeat lapse past 60 s reschedules that worker's in-flight work onto another matching worker under the next attempt number.

clauses.subject: pool-bound
clauses.statement: A deployment's fire pool runs at most 4 units at once, `[control] pool` replacing the bound; a due unit past the bound stays armed and reports pending.
clauses.why: because one bound per deployment caps the process's concurrent pulls, where a bound per exclusion key caps nothing as pipelines are added

clauses.subject: exclusion-key
clauses.statement: A unit's exclusion key is its pipeline id: a unit due while another under its key is in flight starts no second instance, and its next fire recomputes once the first ends.
clauses.why: because two fires of one pipeline race for one cursor

clauses.subject: lease-gated
clauses.statement: A serve process dispatches only while it holds its deployment's cadence lease; a process finding the lease held arms nothing and, under `--cycle`, exits naming the holder.
clauses.why: because two daemons reading one snapshot otherwise fire every due unit twice

clauses.subject: children-reaped
clauses.statement: A serve process starts each child run in its own process group; on `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`, a `--cycle` exit or an unwind it signals each live group `SIGTERM`, `SIGKILL`s the remainder after 10 s, and exits once every child has.
clauses.why: because a child outliving its serve also outlives the cadence lease, and a second scheduler then fires the same pipeline concurrently

clauses.subject: secret-in-document
clauses.statement: A credential value typed into a configuration field raises `SecretMaterialInDocument`; the document holds references and the backend holds material.
clauses.why: because a value in the document reaches every daemon and replica that reads a snapshot

clauses.subject: connector-upload
clauses.statement: An artifact uploaded through the operator surface raises `ConnectorUploadRefused`; the surface references registered connectors by id and version.
clauses.why: because publishing into the registry runs a separate signed path

clauses.subject: version-race
clauses.statement: An apply whose compare-and-swap loses raises `ManifestVersionConflict`, reloads the winning version and reapplies its pending edits onto it, overwriting no applied version.

clauses.subject: validation
clauses.statement: A document failing engine validation raises `ApplyValidationRefused` and claims no version.
clauses.why: because a snapshot store holding a version daemons refuse to arm stalls every daemon reading it

clauses.subject: owner-unconfigured
clauses.statement: An owner with no storage configured or no credential raises `ConfigOwnerUnconfigured`, answered `503`; no local writer substitutes for the store-scoped API.

clauses.subject: weak-conditional-backend
clauses.statement: A configuration owner or catalog backend whose conditional replacement is not linearizable raises `ConditionalWriteUnsupported` at startup or open.

clauses.subject: uninitialized-store
clauses.statement: An edit or apply against a store that has taken no explicit guarded import, an empty store included, raises `StoreNotInitialized`, answered `409`.

clauses.subject: local-claim
clauses.statement: A local control plane validates and claims `manifest@v<N>.toml` in its snapshot directory, `.contextful/control/<project>/` unless `[control] snapshot_dir` names one, on its own; `contextful pipeline apply` is that apply, and no hosted plane sits on its path.
clauses.why: because {{topology.coordinate.air-gap}} holds a single-node deployment to reach no process outside itself

clauses.subject: guarded-import
clauses.statement: `contextful pipeline import` claims v1 from the declared pipelines while the snapshot directory holds no version; a second import claims nothing.

clauses.subject: region-entries
clauses.statement: A residency allow-set holds at most 16 entries.

clauses.subject: region-mismatch
clauses.statement: A configured resource resolving to a region the policy omits raises `EnforceRegionMismatch` at startup, and the runtime serves nothing.

clauses.subject: site-regions
clauses.statement: A push records the pushing site's residency allow-set in the bucket manifest; a push finding a differing set another site recorded, an absent one included, raises `ResidencySitesDiverge` and commits nothing.

clauses.subject: registry-unreadable
clauses.statement: A `CONTEXTFUL_STORES_JSON` value that does not parse raises `StoreRegistryUnreadable` at startup, and no built-in store stands in for the configured set.

clauses.subject: malformed-entry
clauses.statement: One entry that does not decode raises `StoreEntryMalformed` naming it, and is dropped while its siblings are served.

clauses.subject: reserved-id
clauses.statement: A configured entry claiming either built-in id raises `StoreIdReserved`.
clauses.why: because the entry otherwise reads the fixture's rows under its own name

clauses.subject: authored-name
clauses.statement: An entry carrying its own credential or binding name raises `StoreNameAuthored`.

clauses.subject: listing-page
clauses.statement: One listing call answers at most 1000 entries, flags truncation, and counts the keys the read route declines to serve.

clauses.subject: stdio-credential
clauses.statement: Over the process transport a credential is mandatory, a capability token or an explicit owner flag; an unset one raises `StdioCredentialMissing` and does not resolve to the owner context.

clauses.subject: store-selector
clauses.statement: The child's working directory selects the store by walking up to the project manifest; finding none raises `StoreSelectorAbsent` and exits before writing any protocol framing.

clauses.subject: redactor-lookahead
clauses.statement: The streaming redactor buffers 128 chars across each chunk boundary, and no denylist entry is longer than the buffer.
clauses.why: because an identifier split between two chunks otherwise passes unredacted

clauses.subject: unanswerable-suggestion
clauses.statement: A suggested prompt whose answer under these rules is a decline raises `ConsoleSuggestionUnanswerable` when the suggestion set is built.

clauses.subject: ungrounded-answer
clauses.statement: A path composing answer prose in a turn holding no tool result raises `ConsoleUngroundedAnswer`.

clauses.subject: unadmitted-tool
clauses.statement: A call naming a tool the turn's packs do not admit raises `ConsoleToolNotAdmitted` and dispatches nothing.

clauses.subject: mutating-tool
clauses.statement: The visitor-facing endpoint admits a read subset: a client-reachable path naming a write raises `ConsoleMutatingToolRequested`. The one write a turn performs is authored on the server.

clauses.subject: org-face-read-only
clauses.statement: A pack registering a write tool on an organization-wide face raises `ConsoleWriteToolOnOrgFace` at startup, naming the pack and the tool, and the face serves nothing.

clauses.subject: direct-file-read
clauses.statement: A table function resolving a path straight against stored bytes raises `ConsoleFileAccessDirect` on this surface.

clauses.subject: mint-refused
clauses.statement: A refused mint raises `ConsoleTokenExchangeRefused`. A store carrying a shared credential falls back to it; one carrying none surfaces the refusal to the reader.

clauses.subject: sources-per-turn
clauses.statement: A source list carries at most 8 entries.

clauses.subject: planner-reached-memory
clauses.statement: Scaffolding and every deterministic fallback cover data tables; scaffolding naming a memory relation raises `ConsolePlannerReachedMemory`.

clauses.subject: code-path-bounds
clauses.statement: The code path reads at most 5000 rows per data table and stops after 10 s.

clauses.subject: overlay-cache
clauses.statement: The overlay caches for 5 min, a miss included.

clauses.subject: overlay-length
clauses.statement: An overlay is truncated at 8000 chars.

clauses.subject: unparseable
clauses.statement: A vantage that is neither a calendar day nor an instant raises `ConsoleVantageUnparseable`, answered `400`.

clauses.subject: web-bound-unparseable
clauses.statement: A web leg whose bound fails to parse fails that leg and raises `ConsoleWebBoundUnparseable`.

clauses.subject: sample-labels
clauses.statement: A table's arrivals contribute at most 3 entries of sampled label.

clauses.subject: distillation
clauses.statement: After the answer streams, a second pass distils the exchange into at most 3 entries shaped `{subject, key, learning}`, zero included.

clauses.subject: unscoped
clauses.statement: A distilled conclusion landing without the reading-session scope raises `ConsoleLearningUnscoped`.

clauses.subject: client-authored-view
clauses.statement: A view specification arriving from a client, or composed by the model, raises `ConsoleViewNotServerBuilt`.

clauses.subject: component-choice
clauses.statement: One row with one measure draws a metric; a date column with a measure over 3 rows on distinct days draws a line; anything else draws a table offering a bar view.

clauses.subject: absence-is-earned
clauses.statement: The card needs a session with no turns, at present time, a live conclusion, an arrived row matching an interest, and a derivation inside its budget. An error or timeout raises `ConsoleBriefUnavailable`, and no card renders.

clauses.subject: topic-tier
clauses.statement: The topic tier needs at least 2 tokens shared between the conclusion's subject and text and the row's label and topics, one of them naming the subject.

clauses.subject: card-subjects
clauses.statement: A card carries at most 3 subjects.

clauses.subject: articles-per-subject
clauses.statement: A subject carries at most 3 entries of matched article.

clauses.subject: catchup-window
clauses.statement: The backend caps the requested window at 7 d.

clauses.subject: share-affordance
clauses.statement: A surface offering a share control on access-explanation output raises `VisibilityShareAffordance`.

clauses.subject: askerless-audience
clauses.statement: A scheduled job posting to an audience under a service identity raises `VisibilityAskerlessAudience`, naming the destination; a scheduled post's corpus is narrowed in the reviewed manifest to what the destination reaches.

clauses.subject: package
clauses.statement: The policy model is a Lean package rooted at `formal/`: `lakefile.toml` declares one `lean_lib` target and no `require` stanza, and `lean-toolchain` names one exact release string.

clauses.subject: declared-dependency
